info.title: Tools — every layer
info.description: The call contracts of the harness's Tools, one operation per Tool, generated from the Tool nodes (`schemas/tools/tool.ts`) so standard API tooling can read them. **No HTTP server serves these paths**: each Tool is reached as its `x-invoke` says — a command line, an MCP tool, or an in-process call. Tags are the skills each Tool satisfies.

post.description: Assemble every declared `memory` directory's nodes into each agent's memory, per vendor: Claude Code's `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md` (a marked region, injected when the subagent starts) and Antigravity's workspace skill `.agents/skills/<agent>-memory/SKILL.md`. Other vendors (Gemini CLI, Copilot, Codex, Cursor) are not generated.

memory.description: Each agent's assembled memory file, per vendor.

post.summary: Check that an ArchiMate model's fhir-actor tags point at the IG's FHIR ActorDefinitions
post.description: Actors come first: the IG's ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK's personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property `fhir-actor`, whose value is an ActorDefinition's canonical URL, and the IG's ActorDefinitions: FSH `InstanceOf: ActorDefinition` under `input/fsh/`, and FHIR JSON under `fsh-generated/resources/` or `input/resources/`, each canonical being `<sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id>` unless its `url` says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a `#person` actor on an application or technology element, a `#system` actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; `--strict` makes that a failure. `--json` prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name.

instance.description: The layer root whose ArchiMate model is read.

model.description: The model's id from the config.

ig.description: The IG directory holding `sushi-config.yaml` and `input/fsh/`; absent, the layer root.

strict.description: Fail, not only warn, when an ActorDefinition is realized by no element of the model.

json.description: Print the back-links as JSON (element → actors, actor → elements, problems, unrealized) instead of the report.

report.description: The problems, the unrealized ActorDefinitions and a summary line; with `--json`, the back-links as JSON. Exit 1 on any problem, or on an unrealized actor under `--strict`.

x-selection.when: In an IG whose systems are drawn in an ArchiMate model, after its ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK personas: when model authors tag boxes `fhir-actor` in Archi, in CI, and before generating pages that link boxes to actors.
x-selection.limits: Reads one model per run. Checks pointers only: it never creates an ActorDefinition, and an actor missing from the IG is added there, by hand, from its persona. Reads FSH by pattern, not with SUSHI, so an ActorDefinition made only through a RuleSet is not seen until its JSON is generated.
x-selection.cost: One parse of the model and of the IG's FSH; milliseconds. No network, no JVM, no SUSHI.

post.summary: Draw a document's tables and figures from its ArchiMate data, and check the model against the document's relationship rules
post.description: For each table a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` lists under `tables`, rewrites the block's Markdown table from an `archimate-relationship-rules/v1` file (`relationship-rules`: source, relationship, target, note; `relationship-types`: picture, verb, meaning), keeping the caption and footnotes. For each figure under `figures` that names an `svg`, writes the view as SVG (the same drawing as the view's page). For a rules table that names a `model`, reports the rules the model never uses, the relationships no rule covers, the rules ArchiMate's relationship table refuses, and the relationship types the rules use without a meaning. The rules are in charge: nothing is rewritten from the model.

instance.description: The layer root whose config, models, rules and blocks are read.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a block or SVG is not what the data draws.

strict.description: Also exit 1 when the model has relationships no rule covers, or a rule is one ArchiMate does not allow.

blocks.description: The rewritten table blocks and figure SVGs, at the paths the config names; the rules check on stdout.

x-selection.when: When a document's table or figure restates an ArchiMate model (the element and relationship types it uses, the rules between them, a view): generate it instead of typing it, and run `--check` in CI so it cannot drift.
x-selection.limits: Draws relationship tables and view figures only; element-type tables and glossary tables are not covered yet. Checks a relationship's end types only, not derivation chains or viewpoints.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model named, one table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Check a layer's ArchiMate models against its config
post.description: The ArchiMate gate (graph typology `archimate`): every model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names is held, parses (Archi's native XML or its zipped archive), and resolves — every box in every view draws an element the model holds, every relationship's ends are in the model — and no `.archimate` file is held that the config does not name.

instance.description: The layer root whose `archimate` directory is checked.

problems.description: One line per problem on stderr, exit 1; or one ✓ line, exit 0.

x-selection.when: Before publishing a layer's ArchiMate models, and in its CI: a model that will not parse, draws an element it does not hold, or is held without being configured.
x-selection.limits: Archi's native format only; the Open Group exchange format is not read yet.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Count the tangles in ArchiMate views: lines crossing lines, and lines through boxes
post.description: For each view, as `render-view.ts` draws it, count the pairs of lines that cross and the lines that run through a box they do not connect (groups, and boxes that hold one of the line's ends, excepted). With `--view` it lists each tangle by the boxes it joins; with `--max` it is a gate.

model.description: The `.archimate` file (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive).

view.description: One view, by its Archi id (`id-<hex>`) or its page slug (e.g. `1-central-health-workforce-registry`). A slug, not free text, so no shell payload can ride on it. Absent: every view in the model.

max.description: Exit 1 if any view has more tangles than this.

json.description: Print JSON instead of one line per view.

tangles.description: Per view: crossings and lines through a box.

x-selection.when: Before and after every change to an ArchiMate view, so a change never adds tangles (skill `archimate-models`, "Untangle every view you touch").
x-selection.limits: Counts the lines as drawn by this harness's renderer, which draws a stale Archi route straight; Archi itself may draw the same view slightly differently.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per view. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Lower the tangles in ArchiMate views: re-route lines and swap same-size boxes in a row
post.description: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. Without `--apply` it reports before and after per view; with it, the model is written back in place, only the moved boxes' bounds and the re-routed lines' bendpoints changing.

model.description: The `.archimate` file (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive).

view.description: One view, by its Archi id (`id-<hex>`) or its page slug (e.g. `1-central-health-workforce-registry`). A slug, not free text, so no shell payload can ride on it. Absent: every view in the model.

routes-only.description: Never move a box; only re-route lines.

apply.description: Write the model back in place.

json.description: Print JSON instead of one line per view.

report.description: Per view: tangles before and after, and the swaps and routes made.

x-selection.when: After drawing or changing an ArchiMate view, before committing it: run it, look at the drawing, keep what reads better (skill `archimate-models`).
x-selection.limits: A greedy search, one line or one swap at a time: it lowers tangles but does not find the best layout, never adds, resizes or regroups boxes, and leaves lines that end on lines, or share both ends with another line, as they are. The author still looks at the result.
x-selection.cost: Seconds for a large view (about 8 s for 20 views). No network, no JVM.

post.description: Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance's folio-glossary/v1 terms whose `focus` is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their `skosConcept` property (never by name) take the term's prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with `--prune` along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without `--write` it only reports; `--check` fails when anything would change. `--seed` goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under `library/` (`--from`): an authored model is never a source of the glossary.

instance.description: The instance root holding `glossary/*.glossary.json` and `archimate/cat-archimate.config.json`.

model.description: The model's id in the ArchiMate config. Required except with `--seed --from`.

write.description: Write the changes into the model file.

prune.description: Also remove relationships between linked elements that no term lists.

seed.description: Once: give linked terms without a focus the element type and relationships of an INGESTED model (under `library/`). Refused for an authored model.

from.description: With `--seed`: the ingested model file, under the instance's `library/`.

check.description: Fail if the model and the graph disagree.

model.description: The model file, rewritten in place with `--write`.

post.summary: Derive the metamodel an ArchiMate model uses, and check it against ArchiMate's relationship table
post.description: For each model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names: the element types it uses, with counts; every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern its relationships follow, with counts and ids; whether ArchiMate's relationship table (Appendix B of ArchiMate 3.2, as Archi holds it, committed as `archimate/schemas/archimate-relationships.json` in the tools layer) allows each pattern; and the placeholder elements, named after their own type, that a hand-drawn metamodel leaves in a model. Prints a report, JSON, Graphviz DOT or a Mermaid class diagram. `archimate-pages` draws the same result on each model's "Metamodel in use" page, so the metamodel is derived, never drawn.

instance.description: The layer root whose ArchiMate models are read.

model.description: One model's id from the config; absent, every model. Required for `--format dot` and `mmd`.

check.description: Exit 1 when any relationship follows a pattern ArchiMate does not allow. Placeholders are reported, never fatal.

metamodel.description: The report, or the metamodel as `archimate-metamodel/v1` JSON, DOT or Mermaid, on stdout.

x-selection.when: Before publishing an ArchiMate model (process `archimate-publish`, after `archimate-check`), in its CI, and whenever someone asks which element types and relationships a model actually uses — instead of drawing a metamodel view by hand.
x-selection.limits: Checks each relationship's type against its ends' types only; it does not check derivation chains, viewpoints or properties. A type the table does not know is reported as not checked, never as refused.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model and a table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Give every ArchiMate view, element and relationship a page and an IRI, and draw every view
post.description: Write a JSON-LD node and a thin page for each model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names and for every view, element and relationship in it — keyed by Archi's own ids — plus the normalised model the pages' one loader draws from, and every view drawn as SVG from the model's own bounds and bendpoints in ArchiMate's notation, each box a link to its element. `--out` writes into a site being built — the data at the graph's path, the pages at the route of the visualiser the layer declares for this Tool, `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/`; without it the files go into the graph and `--check` gates them.

instance.description: The layer root.

out.description: A site being built: the data lands at `<out>/<graph path>/` and the pages at `<out>/<locale>/<harness>/<id>/`, the route of the layer's one visualiser `renderedBy` this Tool (none declared: nothing is written). Absent, they are written into the graph, which must be `served: true`.

check.description: Without `--out`: fail if a committed page is missing, stale or orphaned; write nothing.

pages.description: Pages and view drawings written (or found current).

x-selection.when: A folio's staging or publish build should show its ArchiMate models: run after the document site is built and before the navbar pass.
x-selection.limits: Draws the notation, not Archi's icons, custom images or fonts; sketch and canvas views are skipped. Never replaced by Archi's CLI report (skill `archimate-models`).
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per view; four models of 5,809 pages and 131 drawings (~24 MB) take about 1.5 s. No network, no JVM.

post.description: Render index pages for the declared skills, docs and swimlane-glossary directories, one per directory.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

scope.description: A scoped site build: the comma-separated instances whose pages this writer writes (the IG and the layer it lands on); every other instance's pages are linked on that layer's own site. Passed by the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts` (owner, 2026-11-08, Q-SZ-2 "B"). Absent: every instance.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.description: Render the declared avatar nodes — an actor's glyph and colours, including the overlay states — into the stylesheet the site serves.

check.description: Compare against the committed copy and fail if stale, instead of writing.

post.summary: Check a bean is free, then claim it on every copy
post.description: For one bean: fetch every bean copy, read the last three commits on its file, skip it if another agent committed within the window or its last note is a claim, look for an open PR naming it in every listed repository, and only then set it in-progress with a dated claim note as a plain commit on every copy. A rejected push is fetched, rebased and re-checked, never forced.

id.description: The bean, full or short id.

copy.description: A local checkout of a bean copy. Repeat once per copy. Defaults to the current checkout.

repo.description: A repository whose open PRs are searched for the id. Repeat. Defaults to the copies' repositories.

minePr.description: The link of an open PR that is the caller's own, when resuming a bean it already holds. Every cloud thread's PR has the same author, so without this any open PR naming the bean is a skip.

as.description: Which agent is asking, by its name in the agents table. Defaults to `cloud`.

session.description: The caller's session link, matched against the `Claude-Session:` trailer so a sibling thread of the same agent is told apart. Defaults to $CLAUDE_SESSION_URL.

agents.description: A JSON file of agents and their commit authors, as in the skill's input schema.

dryRun.description: Check only; report `would-claim` and write nothing.

json.description: Emit `definitions.claimCheck` as JSON.

check.description: One of claimed, would-claim, skip-recent-commit, skip-claim-note, skip-open-pr, skip-closed or unknown, with the evidence per copy and the open PRs found. Exit 0 for claimed or would-claim, 1 for a skip, 2 for unknown. Unknown is never reported as free. With --json, `definitions.claimCheck` of schemas/skills/bean-drain/output.schema.json.

result.description: With --json, the check as one `BeanClaimCheck` record: the state, the evidence per copy and the open PRs found. Programs and BPMN gateways read this; people read `check`.

x-selection.when: Before any work on a bean, when more than one agent may be draining the same store.
x-selection.limits: It sees commits and open PRs, not an agent's intent: an agent that works without committing or opening a PR is invisible until it does. One bean per call. `beans:claim` is the right claim when the store has one copy and no other agents drain it.
x-selection.cost: One fetch and one push per copy, and one paged GitHub REST listing of open PRs per repository.

post.description: Query the beans knowledge graph using named graph analytics or arbitrary SPARQL 1.1.

sparql.description: Arbitrary SPARQL 1.1 SELECT query over the bean store.

format.description: Output format: table, json, or ids.

report.description: Query results formatted as a table, JSON or IDs, for people to read.

result.description: The rows as one `BeanQueryRows` record, each variable to its value with bean IRIs shortened to ids: `structuredContent.rows` over MCP in every format, and the text itself with format json. Programs and BPMN gateways read this; people read `report`.

post.description: Read and write the work plan with the `beans` binary. The normal mechanism when it is installed.

id.description: The bean to act on; absent for list/create.

x-selection.when: The normal case, once `scripts/install-beans.sh` has run. It is the only arm that can answer what an item IS or what it waits on — the fallback gives titles and statuses and nothing else — so any work that involves choosing, claiming or reasoning about an item wants this one.
x-selection.limits: Absent on a fresh container until installed, and the install can fail. It is third-party, which is why `.beans.yml` is one of the two configuration paths `check:harness-dirs` cannot remove. When it is missing, `beans-manual` writes the same store in the same layout and this reads back everything it wrote.
x-selection.cost: One install step per container, and it wants network to fetch. Nothing at runtime after that.

post.description: Read and write the same work plan without the CLI — `scripts/beans-fallback.ts`, or editing a bean's front matter directly. Equal standing to the CLI, not a degraded mode.

x-selection.when: When the CLI is not installed and cannot be — not a rare case: a fresh container has no `beans` on PATH. Equal standing, not a degraded mode. An agent that knows only the CLI reads the plan and touches nothing, which is exactly the 2026-09-18 session that completed two merged PRs' worth of durable work UNCLAIMED.
x-selection.limits: Titles and statuses only. It cannot say what an item is, what it depends on, or what it waits on — enough to CLAIM and to record, not enough to CHOOSE. Install `beans-cli` when the choice is the point.
x-selection.cost: None. The store is files in the repository, so this needs a filesystem and nothing else — which is also why it is the arm that survives an air-gapped or sovereign-compute layer.

post.description: Render every reference in the checkout (each declared `references` directory's folio-reference/v1 nodes and each `catalogue` directory's Dublin Core records) as the bibliography page and one page per sub-graph, each with its BibTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS and Dublin Core JSON-LD exports and a per-reference export, at the route of the visualiser core declares for it.

check.description: Fail if a page or export is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under cat-harness's docs, as a repository's own site build does (`visualiser-writers.ts`).

scope.description: A scoped site build: the comma-separated instances whose pages this writer writes (the IG and the layer it lands on); every other instance's pages are linked on that layer's own site. Passed by the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts` (owner, 2026-11-08, Q-SZ-2 "B"). Absent: every instance.

pages.description: The bibliography pages and their exports, under the published site directory.

post.description: Each labelled block's links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor on `main`, and [feedback] opens a new GitHub issue about the block, from the folio's `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml` when it has one (prefilling only the fields it declares: block, section, source, page, url) or as a plain issue whose body carries the same facts. The document build draws these on every block; this Tool prints them as JSON for one block or all. Governed by the `block-actions` skill.

repo.description: The folio's repository root. Default: the working directory.

block.description: One block's label. Absent: every block of every document. A label no block has exits 1.

github.description: `owner/name` on GitHub. Default `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else the checkout's `origin`. None at all exits 2: no links rather than broken ones.

issue-template.description: The issue form's file name under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. Default `block-feedback.yml`, used only if the folio has it.

links.description: JSON on stdout: one `{ label, source, section, edit, feedback }` per block. A one-line summary goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: A reader, reviewer or agent wants to propose a change to, or give feedback on, one block of a document folio, and needs the link that lands on that block rather than on the repository.
x-selection.limits: Builds URLs; it writes nothing to GitHub. Only labelled blocks get links. The issue form's fields are read by a line scan for `id:`, so a form must declare its ids plainly.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds: one walk of the document manifests. No network.

post.description: Generate, per diagram, a checklist that walks the BPMN as a state machine: each task names the `workflow_complete` call that records it and ends with `next:` by node id; each decision lists its labelled branches (or the DMN that computes it); parallel forks name every branch and joins wait for all; start/end events are entry and exit lines. A rendering, never an authority: it says it is generated, and `--check` fails when one is stale.

out.description: Write every `<stem>.checklist.md` into this one directory instead. Default: each beside its diagram, in the layer that owns it; the harness site's `assets/workflows/checklists` holds those of the layers below the harness.

check.description: Verify instead of write: exit 1 on a stale, missing or orphaned checklist.

checklists.description: One committed `<stem>.checklist.md` per diagram in every layer, beside its `.bpmn`.

x-selection.when: A coding agent needs a process in a form it can follow without reading BPMN XML, or without the engine's MCP server.
x-selection.limits: Conditions are the flows' labels or the DMN's id; a condition expression the model does not carry is not reproduced. The engine stays the authority.
x-selection.cost: One diagram load per process; no network.

post.description: Run a declared BPMN process as an instance: `workflow_start` opens one for a subject, `workflow_next` reports what is enabled, `workflow_complete` records a step or answers a decision (a DMN-computed one from `facts`) and REFUSES a step that is not enabled. State is committed under the work plan, so which edge was taken is a record, not a memory.

process.description: The process to run: a diagram's file stem or its `bpmn:process` id.

node.description: The step or decision to complete, as `workflow_next` reported it.

enabled.description: What may be worked next, after each call.

x-selection.when: Work follows a declared process and its order must be enforced and recorded: a step done out of order should be refused, not just discouraged.
x-selection.limits: Reached over MCP; an agent without the server can walk the generated checklist (`bpmn-checklist`) by hand, but nothing then refuses a wrong turn.
x-selection.cost: One diagram load per call; state is a small committed file.

post.summary: BPMN → Diagram Interchange, laid out by Graphviz
post.description: Lay out a BPMN that carries no Diagram Interchange (`bpmn_to_svg.py` beside this file, moved from `.github/skills/bpmn_layout/` by bean folio-assistant-tgaj): one Graphviz cluster per participant, the coordinates written back into the BPMN as `<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>`, and Graphviz's own SVG. cat-harness-tools' `render:bpmn` draws only the DI a file already has (bpmn-js does not lay out), so this is the step before it for a DAK process written, or imported, without one.

bpmn.description: A BPMN 2.0 file, with or without DI.

svg.description: Graphviz's drawing (`--svg`); not bpmn-js's, so not the published picture.

x-selection.when: A BPMN has no Diagram Interchange, so `render:bpmn` would draw it blank, and a first layout is wanted before an author tidies it (`bpmn:detangle`).
x-selection.limits: A first layout, not the finished one: it does not meet `bpmn-authoring`'s readability rules (fixed task size, label placement, lane order); run `bun run cat bpmn:detangle --write` and look at `render:bpmn`'s picture after it. It parses with the standard library's ElementTree, so it is for files an author holds, not untrusted input.
x-selection.cost: Seconds; needs Graphviz `dot` on the PATH.

post.description: Render each process diagram to SVG for the documentation site. The .bpmn file is the source of truth; the picture is generated from it, so a diagram and its image cannot disagree.

check.description: Fail if any committed SVG is stale, instead of writing.

diagrams.description: The generated SVG directory. Never hand-edited.

post.description: Derive FSH from a DAK's BPMN business processes (the inverse of the extractors).

fsh.description: Generated FSH, for SUSHI to compile.

x-selection.when: An L2 business process is to reach L3 as a computable artefact, not only a picture.
x-selection.limits: Requires a `smart-base` checkout at `SMART_BASE_HOME`; without one the capability is ABSENT, not a clean run.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, plus the upstream checkout.

post.summary: BPMN structure, vendor namespaces and lane → actor
post.description: Check a DAK's BPMN (`validate.ts` beside this file; bean folio-assistant-tgaj, which replaced four Python validators with it): well-formed XML whose root is `<bpmn:definitions>`, no Camunda or Zeebe namespace, no duplicate id, at least one process, no bpmn-moddle (bpmn-js) import warning; every process has a `<laneSet>`, every flow node sits in a lane, and lane ids are unique and valid FSH ids; and every innermost lane names its actor by id: its `partitionElementRef` (a top-level `<bpmn:resource>`), else its own id, matched exactly against the `Instance:` ids of the ActorDefinitions in the IG's FSH (or JSON) and, for a harness process, the role ids of the mounted layers' `scenarios/roles.json`. Never by file name or title. With no file named it reads the declared process directories, `smart-base/**/processes/` and an IG's `input/bpmn/`.

bpmn.description: The .bpmn files to check; when absent, every .bpmn under the declared process directories (or, with `--changed <ref>`, those the branch changed).

fsh.description: Directories of ActorDefinition FSH or JSON; default `input/fsh` and `input/resources`.

roles.description: `scenarios/roles.json` files whose role ids a harness lane may bind; default those of smart-base and the mounted cat-harness, fhir-harness and folio-assistant-core.

report.description: One `✗` line per error and `!` per warning, then a count. Exit 0 no error, 1 an error, 2 nothing to check (not a pass). `--json` prints the findings as data.

x-selection.when: A DAK's business process (L2, BPMN) is added or edited, before review (skill `l2-component-edit-review`, the BPMN row's checker), and on every pull request that changes a `.bpmn`.
x-selection.limits: An ActorDefinition a dependency IG declares is found only when its FSH or JSON directory is passed with `--fsh`. Reads lanes, not pools: a participant whose process has no lanes is reported as a process with no laneSet. A lane bound to a harness role is accepted here; whether that role is equipped is cat-harness's `role-model` check (`kg:audit`). A published DAK whose processes are still Visio figures is crosswalked against its personas by `smart-base/scripts/dak-swimlanes.ts` (always on, beside the `web-annex` kind's `dak-swimlanes/v1` validator), not by this Tool. It does not draw the diagram (`render:bpmn` does) or check DI completeness.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network.

post.summary: Stage one IG as its own just-the-docs Jekyll site
post.description: Turn an IG source repository into ONE Jekyll source for just-the-docs, as the IG Publisher builds one IG per site: `input/pagecontent` pages with title, parent and order from `sushi-config.yaml` `pages:`, the files the Publisher's include tags resolve against, images, `_data/fhir.json` from `ig-site-data`, and a `_config.yml`. The pages render unchanged, including their references to the IG's site data. With the IG's menu, the layout is the one every IG site wears: the IG's own top bar, the IG's TOC declared as the folio-assistant navbar's section (added by `rail-standalone-pages`), no sidebar of its own, an edit link per page, and per heading a source-line link and a pre-filled feedback issue.

out.description: The Jekyll source directory to write.

post.summary: Is CI passing on the default branch?
post.description: Report each workflow's state on the default branch, which a checkout cannot see: a red workflow looks exactly like a green one from in here. One API call over the recent run history, not one request per workflow, so it stays inside the unauthenticated 60/hr limit and stays usable at session start.

markdown.description: Emit the block the session-start sweep prints. ALWAYS exits 0: the sweep runs it as `if ! …; then`, and a non-zero exit would print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red.

warn.description: Report only, never fail. For a caller that wants the state without a verdict.

out.description: Write the markdown report to a file AND keep the exit code — which `--markdown` cannot do, since it always exits 0. Its own flag, so one API call is not spent twice.

report.description: One row per workflow. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, `running`, `superseded` (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or `--out` could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. `--markdown` and `--warn` always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither.

x-selection.when: Before trusting ANY workflow's outcome, and at session start: a workflow's result is invisible from a checkout.
x-selection.limits: It reads the DEFAULT BRANCH, so on a PR it describes `main` and not the diff — which is why it is deliberately not one of the `gates`. `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` is used when present; without one a public repo still works and a private one fails. A REFUSED OR FAILING API CALL EXITS 2 AND IS NEVER GREEN: could-not-look must stay distinguishable from looked-and-it-was-fine.
x-selection.cost: One HTTP request; fast enough for the session-start sweep, which is why it makes a single call.

post.description: Draw a paper's block graph from buildContentGraph: chapters as packages, editorial edges (uses / interprets) solid and formal Lean edges (type / value) dashed purple, never one derived from the other, and each block filled by its formalization status from proof-objects.json when given. One diagram for the paper and one per chapter, each in portrait and landscape, stamped with its source's hash. Run from a folio: the platform carries no paper.

root.description: The folio's content directory, where the block manifests are.

out.description: Where to write the .puml files and their SVGs.

status.description: proof-objects.json, for status fills. Without it every block is drawn unfilled.

check.description: Fail if a diagram or SVG is stale or orphaned, instead of writing. Needs no Java.

diagrams.description: content-graph.puml and content-graph/<chapter>.puml, with portrait and landscape SVGs beside them.

post.description: Validate the block manifests under a path against their schemas.

targetPath.description: A paper or chapter directory; absent, every paper the folio declares.

issues.description: One line per issue, with its block and file. Exit 2 means NO FOLIO WAS FOUND — could-not-determine, never valid.

post.description: Check every committed JSON-LD document that names the content context, or a layer's own generated context: every plain key is a declared term (never descending into an `@json` value), and no file path sits under an `@id`-coerced term. An empty corpus is a finding, never a clean run. Prefixes are checked by `jsonld:contexts --check`.

json.description: Emit both reports as JSON instead of the console summary.

report.description: Console (or JSON) report; exit 1 on an undeclared key, a path under an `@id` term, or an empty corpus.

post.summary: Search the corpus and follow the graph
post.description: Seed lexically over the authored folio and every declared library, then expand along graph edges, labelling each hit MATCHED or REACHED and by which edge. Counts are split authored vs ingested, and a root that exists but holds no graph nodes is reported rather than read as an empty answer.

query.description: Words to seed on. Seeding is lexical, so a short phrase works; a long query no node contains seeds nothing.

hops.description: Expansion depth, 0-4 (default 1). 0 is a plain lexical search.

provenance.description: `authored` or `ingested`: restricts the seeds, not the expansion.

searchText.description: Also seed on companion Markdown bodies.

result.description: JSON: summary, emptyRoots, dangling, and hits each carrying a `why`.

post.description: Generate `dak-api.html`, the DAK API's entry page, and the per-artefact `.openapi.json` / `.displays.json` sidecars.

x-selection.when: The DAK API is to have a reader-facing entry point.
x-selection.limits: `dak-api.html` links its schemas to a `schemas/` directory that does not hold the root enumeration schemas. Resolve a sidecar from the index, never by composing the hub's path.
x-selection.cost: The largest upstream script; runs inside the publisher container against the full output.

post.description: Derive the DAK configuration from `sushi-config.yaml` plus repository and branch context.

branch.description: Sanitised branch name, for the publication and preview URLs.

x-selection.when: A DAK repository has no configuration yet, or its branch context has changed.
x-selection.limits: Upstream runs it twice, before and after the branch name is sanitised, as an ordering workaround. Run it once, after sanitising.
x-selection.cost: Seconds. The whole DAK phase is gated on the file it writes, so a silent failure disables every later step.

post.summary: Every path a declaration names resolves — directories, assets, visualisers, needs
post.description: Read every layer declaration in the checkout and resolve what it names: `directories` (and those declared from within) through `check:declared-dirs`, `assets` through `check:declared-assets`, `visualisers[].renderedBy` through `check:visualiser-routes`, `needs` through the instance-graph resolver, and `visualisers[].coversKinds` against the graph typologies registered IN THIS CHECKOUT — its own and those a mounted layer contributes, read from the checkout under inspection rather than from where the harness module sits. A declaration that does not parse is a finding. One verdict per layer and field, naming the gate that decided it. Exit 0 every reference resolves, 1 one does not, 2 could not determine; a certain finding is reported before anything undetermined.

root.description: The checkout to check; the script re-runs itself there, so kinds are read from it. Default: the working directory.

json.description: Print the report as JSON.

findings.description: Unresolved references per layer and field, and what could not be determined; entries examined per field.

post.summary: DIIG phases, steps and resources chart
post.description: Draw a DIIG "phases, steps and resources" chart as SVG from `diig-phases-figure/v1` data on a who-iris library entry (DIIG Fig. 1.1.1, or a handbook's republished version such as the product catalogue handbook's Fig. 4), or from a folio's `diig-phases-adaptation/v1` file that adds its own tiles and marks itself "(this document)". Every label comes from the data; tiles link to their library entry or glossary concept.

figure-or-adaptation.description: A diig-phases-figure/v1 file, or a diig-phases-adaptation/v1 file whose `adapts` is a repository-root path to one.

out.description: Where to write the SVG; stdout when absent.

svg.description: The chart, with text as SVG text, one `<g id="tile-<resource>">` per tile.

x-selection.when: A folio shows the DIIG phases chart (every Digital Transformation Handbook does) and should draw it from the one transcription instead of a picture or a hand-kept copy.
x-selection.limits: Draws the seven-row DIIG layout only. Whether the transcription matches the published figure is a person's review of the data.
x-selection.cost: Reads one or two JSON files; no network.

post.description: Put a question to a person or a sibling agent and receive an answer, to determine which harness this repository should become and which repositories are read from and written to. The two facts no file holds.

question.description: The question as put, with its candidates named. One question where one will do.

askedOf.description: `person` or `agent` — symmetric participants, recorded because the answers are evidence of different weight.

answer.description: The reply as received. Absent is a real result: it routes to `outcome: unsettled`, never to a guess.

x-selection.when: A fact is needed that no file in reach holds — which harness, or which repositories. Narrow the candidates from context first; a repository already carrying `cat-harness/cat-harness.json` is not a blank slate, and a question the agent could have answered itself wastes the one it is entitled to.
x-selection.limits: It cannot manufacture an answer. A participant may decline, and that is `outcome: unsettled` with what is still open — not an error and not a default. An agent that reaches for a documented default because nobody replied has produced a guess.
x-selection.cost: One round trip through a person's attention, which is the most expensive input in the system and the reason the skill's rule is to ask once.

post.description: Render each DMN decision table to an HTML fragment for a page, via `dmn2html.xslt` and `dmn.css`.

html.description: One HTML fragment per decision table.

x-selection.when: A reader needs to see a decision table as a table.
x-selection.limits: Its output is HTML, which the JSON-only render contract (`ig-render-jekyll`) does not accept as a representation. Whether the just-the-docs pipeline gets a structured output from it or carries the HTML as an embedded asset is undecided.
x-selection.cost: Seconds; needs `lxml` for the XSLT.

post.description: Generate FHIR `Questionnaire` resources from a DAK's DMN decision tables. Authoring, not rendering: the IG Publisher validates and indexes them like any other resource.

dmnDir.description: The DMN source directory, by convention `input/dmn/`.

questionnaires.description: The generated `Questionnaire` resources, written beside SUSHI's output.

generated.description: How many were produced. Zero means none only when the DMN directory was found; a missing directory is reported as such.

x-selection.when: A DAK carries DMN decision tables and the IG is to expose them as answerable questionnaires.
x-selection.limits: Reads DMN only: a decision expressed only in prose or CQL is skipped without error. It cannot tell an empty DMN directory from a DAK with no decisions.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network. It runs before the Publisher, so a failure noticed only downstream costs a build cycle.

post.description: Render each declared document-kinds directory: every kind's structure, sections and sources, one page per subject layer.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.description: Read every bean copy, keep the drainable open beans (task, bug, feature in todo or in-progress, not blocked, not owner-held), group them by the owner already working in that area, mark the ones another agent touched within the window as skip, and list everything left out with its reason and every bean whose copies disagree. The newest updated_at wins where copies disagree.

copy.description: A local checkout of a bean copy, fetched by the tool to its bean ref. Repeat once per copy. Defaults to the current checkout.

holdings.description: A JSON file mapping each owner to the bean ids it holds (`holdings` in the skill's input schema).

agents.description: A JSON file of the agents and their commit authors (`agents` in the skill's input schema). Defaults to the table in the bean-drain skill.

window.description: Another agent's commit within this window marks a bean skip. Defaults to 24h.

json.description: Emit the queue as JSON matching `definitions.queue`, instead of Markdown.

queue.description: The queue: sources with the tip each was read at, one section per owner in priority order, the spare pool, the excluded beans with reasons, and the copies that disagree. With --json, the same as `definitions.queue` of schemas/skills/bean-drain/output.schema.json. A copy that cannot be fetched is an error, never an empty queue.

result.description: With --json, the queue as one `DrainQueue` record: sources, owner sections in priority order, the spare pool, exclusions and disagreeing copies. Programs read this; people read `queue`.

x-selection.when: Starting or refreshing a drain with more than one agent, or giving an idle drainer its next beans.
x-selection.limits: It proposes; it does not claim. Every bean taken from it still goes through `bean-claim-check`. Owner-held is read from the last note's wording and can miss; a person reviewing the queue is the backstop. For one agent picking one bean, `bean-query` named `safe_drain_candidates` is enough.
x-selection.cost: One fetch per copy and one `git log` per open bean. No GitHub API calls.

post.description: Render every `folio-dublin-core/v1` record a catalogue item names as Dublin Core XML (qualified DC, per DCMI's XML guidelines) and as JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Both are written into the instance's published root (`<instanceRoot>/dublin-core/<stem>.dc.xml` and `.dc.jsonld`), so the site mount publishes them beside the item pages. Deterministic. `--check` fails on a missing, stale or orphaned rendering. Governed by the `dublin-core-renderings` skill.

instance.description: The catalogue instance's root, e.g. an IRIS mirror's directory. It must hold `catalogue/catalogue.json` and declare a directory with `instanceRoot: true`.

check.description: Write nothing. Exit 1 if any rendering is missing, stale or orphaned.

renderings.description: `<published root>/dublin-core/`: one `.dc.xml` and one `.dc.jsonld` per record. A one-line summary goes to stdout.

x-selection.when: A catalogue record changed, a catalogue item was added or removed, or the DCMI mapping changed. The renderings must then be regenerated before the gate passes.
x-selection.limits: Renders only records a catalogue item names. Fields with no DCMI term keep a minted predicate in JSON-LD and are reduced to their DC element in XML. A non-`dc` schema field cannot appear in XML at all, and is listed in a header comment. Not OAI-PMH `oai_dc`.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per record. Reads the catalogue nodes and records; no network.

post.description: Render the declared external schemas, and which of this instance's modules conform to each, as one page.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.summary: DAK spreadsheets → DMN, PlanDefinitions, CQL, requirements, logical models
post.description: Run WHO's `extract_dak.py` in a DAK or IG repository. It reads the DAK template spreadsheets (`input/decision-logic/*.xlsx` via `dt_extractor`, `input/system-requirements/*.xlsx` via `req_extractor`, `input/dictionary/*.xlsx` via `dd_extractor`) and the BPMN, and writes DMN decision tables, CPG recommendation PlanDefinitions with citations, CQL library skeletons, Requirements and logical-model FSH. Per the WHO IG Starter Kit (`l3_decisiontables`, `l3_cql`), an adapted decision or scheduling table is an edited copy of the upstream DAK's spreadsheet, never a parallel format.

dakRepository.description: The working directory: a DAK or IG repository with `input/decision-logic/`, `input/system-requirements/` and `input/dictionary/` spreadsheets in the DAK template layout.

dmn.description: Decision tables in the DAK DMN format (namespace `https://www.omg.org/spec/DMN/20240513/MODEL/`), each with an `Annotations` and a `Reference(s)` output.

fsh.description: PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, Requirements and logical-model FSH, for SUSHI to compile.

cql.description: CQL library skeletons, one per decision table, with the definitions already present in `input/cql/` carried over.

x-selection.when: An L2 decision-support, scheduling, requirements or data-dictionary component is created or adapted and the upstream DAK keeps it in the WHO DAK spreadsheet template. Look for that spreadsheet upstream before writing a decision table by hand.
x-selection.limits: Reads only the DAK template layout (COVER sheet, per-tab inputs and outputs); a table in any other shape is invisible to it. Requires a `smart-base` checkout at `SMART_BASE_HOME`; without one the capability is ABSENT, not a clean run. Where the upstream DAK repository has its own converters (e.g. `tools/node/processDT*.js` in https://github.com/litlfred/smart-immunizations), use those.
x-selection.cost: Seconds to minutes, no network unless `--run-publisher` is passed.

post.description: Publish a branch's built site to `branches/<slug>/` on the publish branch, so a reviewer compares a rendered before and after rather than a description of one. Stamps the commit SHA, and removes the preview when its pull request closes.

branch.description: The branch to stage; blank stages the current one. On a pull request the workflow fires by itself and needs none of these.

cleanup_slug.description: DELETION: the `branches/<slug>` to remove, instead of staging anything. For an orphan preview the health sweep reports: its pull request is already closed, so the close event cannot remove it.

cleanup_confirm.description: The slug again, exactly. Anything else refuses, so a confirmation cannot carry over to a DIFFERENT preview, which a boolean would allow.

x-selection.when: On a pull request touching the docs, schemas, content or skills it fires on its own — reach for the dispatch arm only to stage a branch that has no open pull request, or to remove a preview the close event could not reach.
x-selection.limits: The removal arm is guarded THREE ways: `workflow_dispatch` is available only to an actor with write access; `cleanup_confirm` must repeat the slug exactly; and the removal is preflighted at removal time against the same liveness signals the health sweep uses: `deletion-requires-confirmation` applied to the tool most able to break it. This node does not claim that skill, because implementing the discipline once is not the same as stating it.
x-selection.cost: A full site build plus a push to the publish branch. Concurrency is keyed on the branch or the cleanup slug, NOT the shared ref, so two cleanups of different previews do not cancel each other.

post.summary: Seed the FHIR package cache from trusted sources (exact versions)
post.description: Fill `~/.fhir/packages` (or `--cache`) for an environment that cannot reach packages.fhir.org, from trust anchors only: npm account `grahamegrieve`, publishers' own published-site repositories (the seeder's list, each fetch verified against the tarball's own package.json), template repos found through FHIR/ig-registry's templates.json read live each run, and a `--mirror`. Exact versions only (a patch wildcard resolves as the Publisher resolves it, recorded); every tarball verified; nothing computed once and kept; provenance recorded; missing versions listed, never substituted.

sushi-config.description: Seed what this IG pins: its `dependencies:` and the core package for its `fhirVersion`.

lock.description: An IG's `fhir-packages.lock.json` (`packages`: name, version, `tarball` https URL, `integrity` sha512-/sha256- and/or hex `sha256`). Each package it pins is installed from that URL only, after every pinned hash matches; a mismatch is refused. Its dependencies are not followed: the lock lists them.

cache.description: Default `~/.fhir/packages`, which SUSHI and the IG Publisher read.

mirror.description: A directory or git repository of `<name>#<version>.tgz` filled by `fhir-package-mirror`.

missing-out.description: Write the missing list, one `name#version` per line: the input `fhir-package-mirror` takes.

missing.description: Exit 1 when any is missing. Each is listed with why: not on npm, a different version only, an untrusted maintainer, or not an exact version.

x-selection.when: packages.fhir.org is unreachable and registry.npmjs.org is not.
x-selection.limits: Pinned HL7 versions are often not on npm and need `--mirror`. A template FHIR/ig-registry does not list is named with `--template-repo`. A partly seeded cache does not make a faithful build of an IG whose pins it misses.
x-selection.cost: One download per package; the core packages are tens of megabytes.

post.summary: Load the stable FHIR releases' core StructureDefinitions as a graph keyed by canonical URL
post.description: Read each stable FHIR release's core package (`hl7.fhir.r4.core#4.0.1`, `hl7.fhir.r4b.core#4.3.0`, `hl7.fhir.r5.core#5.0.0`) at the version, sha1 and sha512 `fhir-core/pins.json` pins, and keep its resources, complex and primitive types and root types (Base, Element, BackboneElement, DomainResource, Resource) under `fhir-core/<release>/`, keyed by canonical URL. `index` writes the release's manifest (each definition's kind, type, base and sha256); `materialise` writes the bodies byte for byte as the package holds them; `check` holds the two to the pins offline; `resolve` answers which file a canonical URL is kept in. A package that cannot be fetched or verified is recorded as `unread` with the reason, never as an empty graph.

root.description: The fhir-harness layer root. Default: the layer this script is in.

release.description: One release (R4, R4B or R5). Default: every pinned release.

tgz-dir.description: A directory of already-downloaded `<name>-<version>.tgz`; still hash-checked against the pin.

definitions.description: Definitions indexed or materialised per release; an unread release is named with its reason.

x-selection.when: Before a reader resolves a FHIR core type by canonical URL (a class diagram of an IG's logical models or profiles), or when a pin changes.
x-selection.limits: Stable releases only. Constraint profiles, extension definitions and logical models in the core package are left out and counted.
x-selection.cost: One 13-17 MB download per release, then seconds; `check` and `resolve` are offline.

post.summary: Mirror FHIR packages from packages.fhir.org into a git repository
post.description: On a machine that reaches packages.fhir.org, fetch exactly a missing list (from `fhir-cache-seed-npm --missing-out`), check each tarball names itself exactly, record SHA512SUMS, and commit and push to a git repository that an environment without packages.fhir.org reads with `--mirror`. The person running it is the trust anchor for what it adds.

mirror-repo-dir.description: A git checkout to fill; committed and pushed when it is one.

missing.description: The seeder's `--missing-out` file, so nothing unneeded is mirrored.

mirrored.description: Exit non-zero when any could not be fetched or named itself differently.

x-selection.when: The seeder reports missing packages and the environment that needs them cannot reach packages.fhir.org.
x-selection.limits: Run where packages.fhir.org is reachable. It mirrors exact versions only; a wildcard in the list is resolved by the seeder first.
x-selection.cost: One download per package; terminology packages are megabytes each.

post.description: For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). Exits non-zero when any declared figure is missing; `--require-computable` also fails on pictures, linked or not.

entry.description: The L1 library entry directory; its `sections/*.md` give the declared figures, read with cat-harness-tools `declaredFigureCaptions`.

folio.description: The folio's document directory; every figure, diagram and table block naming a figure is read.

exclusions.description: JSON `[{figure, scope: block|rebuild, reason, signedOffBy?, signedOffAt?}]`. Without `signedOffBy` an exclusion is a proposal and does not count.

out.description: Where to write the report; stdout when absent.

report.description: A `figure-coverage-report/v1` JSON report: declared count, counts per state, one row per figure with its blocks, blocks naming undeclared figures, and problems. A per-figure table goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: A folio has been seeded from an L1 library entry (for example a Digital Transformation Handbook), and somebody needs to know that every figure the publication declares has a block, and which are still only pictures.
x-selection.limits: Figure numbers come from block captions and the first line of each block's Markdown. Whether a rebuild is faithful is a person's review, not this check.
x-selection.cost: Reads an entry's sections and a folio's blocks; no network.

post.description: Summarise a folio's committed per-block QA verdicts into one `block-qa.json` a staging preview publishes: each block is failing (a FRESH verdict failed, with the worst severity), stale (a verdict predates the block's current files), passing, or unaudited. Freshness is the QA sweep's own rule, including the uses-graph hash for graph-scoped criteria. Runs no checker and writes no verdict.

out.description: Where to write `block-qa.json`.

repo.description: The folio's instance root, where verdicts are anchored. Default: found from `folio` exactly as the QA sweep finds it.

block-qa.description: A `folio-block-qa-summary/v1` file keyed by block label. Its counts go to stderr.

x-selection.when: A staging preview is being built and its review page's heat map should show QA per section, from what the folio's QA sweep last recorded.
x-selection.limits: Reports the LAST sweep: in a staging build, the sweep the job ran just before it; otherwise the committed verdicts. A folio never swept reads unaudited throughout. Verdicts are read at the instance root, so a folio in a subfolder is read at its own root, then in the folio directory.
x-selection.cost: One text walk of the folio and one read per sidecar. No network.

post.description: Picture each changed figure, diagram, table, equation or simulator block on the published main site and on a staging build, and compare the two pictures pixel by pixel in Chromium's canvas. Writes `visual-diff.json` (`folio-visual-diff/v1`: per block, the share of pixels changed beyond anti-aliasing, and the before, after and diff pictures) and `visual/*.png`, which the review page's visual renderer shows. A side that cannot be pictured (page or anchor missing) is recorded as missing, never drawn blank. Drives Chromium through Playwright.

changeset.description: The preview's `changeset.json`: which blocks changed, and their kind on each side.

base.description: The published main site, as a directory (the publish branch's root).

out.description: Where to write `visual-diff.json` and `visual/`: the site root, so the review page finds them.

count.description: Print how many changed blocks would be pictured, and stop, so a caller installs a browser only when there is work.

visual-diff.description: `<out>/visual-diff.json` and `<out>/visual/*.png`. A per-block summary goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: A staging build changed a figure, diagram, table, equation or simulator, whose markup diff says little, and the reviewer needs to see before and after.
x-selection.limits: The number is how MUCH changed, never whether the change is right. A block's picture is its anchor down to the next anchor, so a page whose anchors are missing or misplaced pictures the wrong region. Pictures are of the light theme.
x-selection.cost: A Chromium launch and two page loads, one screenshot and one canvas compare per visual block. Nothing when no visual block changed.

post.description: What changed in a folio between two git refs, block by block: each block added, removed, or changed — and for a changed block, every aspect that applies (renamed, prose, manifest, moved). Keyed on the block label, which the `id-unique` / `id-stable` QA criteria guard, not on file paths.

folio.description: The folio's `folio` graph directory, relative to the repository — what `<slug>.json` declares for it, usually `folio/`.

base.description: The ref compared against. Default `origin/main`. An unresolvable base is an ERROR, never an empty ChangeSet.

head.description: The ref under review, or `worktree` (the default) for the files on disk, uncommitted edits included.

out.description: Where to write the JSON. Absent: stdout.

text-out.description: Also write `changeset-text.json`: the prose, source and rendered, of every block the ChangeSet lists, on each side that has it. The review page's diff renderers read it.

changeset.description: A `folio-changeset/v1` document. Its one-line summary goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: A reviewer, or the review page, needs to know which BLOCKS a branch changed — not which files. Use it before building a before/after table, a change heat map, or a per-block diff report.
x-selection.limits: Reads manifests as text and never executes the base ref, so a section whose blocks are computed rather than listed is invisible to it. An unlabelled block is identified by its slug, so renaming its file reads as removed plus added. Rendered assets (SVGs) are not compared.
x-selection.cost: Seconds for a few thousand blocks: one `git archive` per committed ref, then a text walk. No network.

post.description: Create a new folio repository that uses this platform — folio/, uploads/, library/, the first manifests, the builder shim, agent files, and the link back to the platform.

authors.description: One entry per author. Repeated rather than a joined string: a name may contain the separator.

assistant_path.description: Path to the platform checkout, for a sibling link.

report.description: What was written, or what would have been under --dry-run.

post.description: A review-process task moves one `review-comment/1.0.0` todo's status (address, send back, resolve, adjudicate, withdraw) through `transition()`, which refuses any move the named BPMN task may not make. The comment is written to the folio's todos graph (its declared `todo-feedback` directory) and, with `--commit`, committed to the edit-set's FEATURE branch. Refused on the base branch and on a detached HEAD.

to.description: The status to move it to: open, addressed, resolved, adjudicated or withdrawn, checked by the script against that closed list.

process.description: The BPMN process whose task is making the move.

task.description: The task, in that process, making the move.

decision.description: The Decision that closes it. Required to resolve or adjudicate.

todos.description: The folio's todos graph root. Default `todos`.

published.description: The published `review-comments.json`, for a comment not committed yet.

commit.description: Commit the file to the current feature branch.

base.description: The base branch a status may NOT be committed to. Default `main`.

x-selection.when: An editor or adjudicator, acting in a review-process task, has decided what happens to a reviewer's comment and the decision must be recorded where the edit is: on the feature branch.
x-selection.limits: Only the moves in `REVIEW_TRANSITIONS`, and only by the task each names. Anchor facts in a committed file are those of the last move; the published file is where re-anchoring shows.
x-selection.cost: Reads one directory and writes one file; one git commit with `--commit`.

post.description: Ingest a pull request's tagged conversation comments (`block: <label>` on the first line) into `review-comment/1.0.0` todos, and write them as `review-comments.json`. Idempotent over its previous output, whose statuses it keeps. Re-anchors every comment against the head's blocks, following `renamedFrom`, and orphans a comment whose block is gone rather than dropping it.

repo.description: `owner/name` of the repository the pull request is in.

out.description: Where to write `review-comments.json`.

folio.description: Read the head's blocks from the folio's manifests (as text; nothing is executed). Give this OR `blocks`.

blocks-out.description: With `folio`: also write `blocks.json`, so a later run can anchor without checking the folio out.

blocks.description: A published `blocks.json`. The comment-triggered refresh uses this, so it never checks out the pull request's code.

existing.description: The previous `review-comments.json`. Every comment in it is kept, with its status.

post.summary: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
post.description: Before a model reads a sub-agent's report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are `control` (steers what the receiver does) or `data` (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator's plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. Exit 0 clean, 1 refused, 3 quarantined, 2 could not determine.

x-selection.cost: Reads the manifest and dependency document once.

post.summary: Measure the AST export on real IGs
post.description: Build the WHO SMART Trust and Immunizations IGs through `ig-ast-export` and print the fork's measurements: counts, whether FSH sources sit where the plan expects, and logic-layer edge coverage per resource type. `--byte-identical` adds a stock build and an `output/` diff.

post.summary: Write the IG AST viewer: a page per instance holding `ig-ast` directories, and a hub
post.description: For every visualiser an instance declares `renderedBy: ig-ast-pages`, write the hub at `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, with `subgraphs: "instance"`, one page per instance that declares an `ig-ast` directory, at `…/<instance>/`. Each lists the ASTs the directory holds: the IG's package id, resources in total and by type, dependency edges (resolved inside the IG, by origin, by kind), the rebuild plan when one is recorded, and what stays provisional. A declared directory not on disk — a branch-family member not restored, which is the normal case — is reported UNKNOWN with the family it would be restored from, never as zero ASTs. `ig-ast-list` summarises one AST it is handed; this Tool needs no AST path.

site.description: A site being built: the pages go under it (`visualiser-writers.ts` in cat-harness-tools passes it). Absent, they go under the checkout's site directory.

root.description: The checkout whose declarations are read. Default: the checkout holding the working directory.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a page is stale, missing or orphaned.

pages.description: Pages written: the hub and one per instance.

x-selection.when: Publishing a site that should show which IG ASTs each instance holds.
x-selection.limits: Counts what the cache holds; it does not check an AST against its IG's inputs (`ig-ast-validity` does) or diff two (`ig-ast-diff`).
x-selection.cost: Reads each AST's manifest and dependency document once.

post.summary: Plan an incremental IG build from a delta of changed files
post.description: Map a delta (a commit range, a PR's diff, or the staged index) onto a base AST: which resources to rebuild (the forward cone), which to load from cache, which to remove, or a full build and why. Builds nothing.

head.description: Default HEAD; `-staged` diffs the index instead.

fsh-users.description: `fsh-file-users/v1` from `fsh-cone --file-users`: lets a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file reach its users rather than force a full build.

rebuild.description: The forward cone. The plan says `full`, with reasons, when a file's effect cannot be determined or the cone exceeds the threshold.

x-install.cli: git clone -b claude/ast-export https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher && cd fhir-ig-publisher/ast-export && mvn -q package && mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=cp.txt
