x-selection.limits: The cone is computed on the BASE edges, so it is provisional until the rebuild: new edges can extend it. A RuleSet-only FSH file forces a full build unless `-fsh-users` is given.
x-selection.cost: Seconds; reads files and git.

post.summary: Refresh an IG's AST cache on a runner
post.description: Dispatch an IG repository's `ig-ast-refresh.yml`, which calls fhir-harness's reusable `.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml`: mount the layers the IG's index.lock.json pins, restore and judge the cache for `ref`, and when it is not valid (or `force`) run the caller's optional `pre-export` overlay command and build the IG with the pinned Publisher AST exporter (the AST is recorded against the clean commit's inputs, the overlay's changes put back), check the new AST is valid for its commit, and seed `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>` with `ig-cache seed --push` — only from a commit on the default branch with the tip's inputs. Builds no site, writes no gh-pages, dispatches nothing.

repository.description: The IG repository that carries the caller (`owner/repo`).

ref.description: What to build; default `main`. Only a commit on the default branch with the tip's inputs is seeded.

force.description: Rebuild even when the cache is valid.

result.description: The run's verdict before (`valid`, `stale`, `cannot-tell`, `missing`) and whether it seeded; the AST as a run artifact when it did not.

x-invoke.shell: gh workflow run ig-ast-refresh.yml --repo <owner/repo> --ref main -f ref=main [-f force=true]

x-selection.when: An IG site publish refused a stale or missing AST, or the IG's source changed on its default branch. Dispatched by a person, or by an agent the owner named for that run — never by an agent on its own.
x-selection.limits: Needs the IG repository to carry the caller and an index.lock.json that mounts fhir-harness. A merge that changes an input during the build leaves the cache unseeded (the run says so). A `pre-export` command is the caller's, in its own workflow file, never a dispatch input; a failing one exports nothing. The no-shrink gate refuses a candidate under 90% of the incumbent.
x-selection.cost: One GitHub runner for the Publisher build: about 25 minutes cold for a ~700-resource IG, less with the restored txcache.

post.summary: Render a computed IG AST delta as just-the-docs pages
post.description: Write the pages for a delta already computed by `ig-ast-diff --json`: an index that lists, a page per changed resource that shows, every one opening with the provisional mark and with Liquid in values neutralised.

x-selection.when: Re-rendering a stored delta without the two ASTs, e.g. into a staging site.
x-selection.limits: Shows what the delta records; it cannot add a differential the delta did not compute.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per page.

post.summary: Is this IG AST still valid for the IG's current inputs?
post.description: Run folio-assistant-core's `compiledValidity` on an AST manifest's `inputs`: recompute the input digest (the same algorithm as the Java writer, pinned by a shared golden vector) and the source revision, and answer valid, stale-inputs (naming which input), or cannot-tell.

toolchain.description: The Publisher that would run now. Without it the toolchain is ASSUMED unchanged, and the result says so.

verdict.description: Exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs, 2 cannot-tell. Cannot-tell is never a pass.

x-selection.when: Before trusting, planning against, or rendering from a cached AST.
x-selection.limits: Valid means built from these inputs, not built correctly.
x-selection.cost: Reads `input/` once to hash it.

post.summary: Measure the IG Publisher's binary outputs on a pages branch
post.description: Read a pages branch's git tree and report the Publisher's binary outputs (full-ig.zip, package.tgz and variants, package.db, validator packs, the definitions/examples/expansions zips, spreadsheets) by name: copies, bytes, and how much of it sits in branch previews. Reads the tree, never a checkout, so a multi-gigabyte branch costs a depth-1 fetch.

repo.description: A clone that has the pages branch fetched.

ref.description: Default `origin/gh-pages`.

x-selection.when: Before configuring an IG's deploy or release step, when a pages branch nears its size limit, or before linking a download from a page.
x-selection.limits: Counts only the Publisher's own binary names; another large file is in `total` but not itemised. It measures, and deletes nothing.
x-selection.cost: One `git ls-tree` over the branch; seconds for 64,000 files.

post.description: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt AST artefacts for an IG. Always try `restore` first: a full AST build via AstExportCli is expensive, a restore is fast. `seed` commits the IG API a layer above generates from the AST (`ig-site:sidecars`, via `ig-api-cache.ts`) as `ig-api/` beside it, and the artefact index built from that tree (`ig-index-cache.ts`) as `fhir-artifact-index/index.json`, so a site reads both by raw URL at the cache commit.

action.description: The verb. `doctor` diagnoses a restore that missed.

igRoot.description: The IG whose AST is acted on.

remote.description: Git remote to fetch from / push to. Default 'origin'. Use when the IG's origin is upstream and the cache lives on a fork.

result.description: A real hit, a miss, or a diagnosis — never a miss that reads as a hit.

post.summary: Build and publish an IG repository's own site with its folio-site.yml workflow
post.description: Dispatch the IG repository's `folio-site.yml` (copied from the IG layer's `ig-repo-site` template): on a runner it composes the harness chrome for THIS layer (`compose-docs --shell --instance`, `gen-navbar-include`), composes the IG at the root of that Jekyll shell (`stage-ig-sites --compose-at-root`), builds it with Jekyll so every IG page wears the theme's side bar, search box and icon row, publishes the layer's served directories, rails any page Jekyll did not lay out (`rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance`), stamps the platform that built it (`folio-build.json`), and on the default branch deploys the whole site to the `gh-pages` root. It reports platform drift against sibling sites and re-dispatches the IGs this one depends on when a token allows.

repo.description: The IG repository whose workflow to dispatch. Default: the current repository.

ref.description: The branch to build. Only the default branch deploys; any other builds and reports.

status.description: The dispatch, and the run it starts; the site is served once that run and GitHub's Pages deploy have finished.

x-selection.when: A pipeline that carries `folio-site.yml` and builds on a runner rather than in the agent's checkout. `stage-local` gives an IG the same site — theme side bar and search, served directories, stamp — from the agent's checkout.
x-selection.limits: Dispatch-only and runner-bound: it needs a runner, the `gh` CLI with a token that may run workflows, and the folio-assistant submodule the template expects. It builds the IG with `stage-ig-sites`, not the IG's own `ghbuild.yml`, and has no plan or dry-run: a run on the default branch deploys. The agent pipeline does not use it.
x-selection.cost: One runner job, 8 to 15 minutes, plus GitHub's Pages deploy.

post.summary: Build each IG instance's artefact index from the IG's cached AST
post.description: Write each IG instance's `fhir-artifact-index/` at publish, so no IG instance commits one. Indexes each instance that needs this layer and whose `repository` has an AST cache branch; others are skipped and named. Per instance: `index.json` from the AST `ig-cache.sh restore` lays down from the IG repository's cache branch (`authority: "cache"`), `menu.json` from the IG's `sushi-config.yaml` at the commit cloned (recording the `source.of` and `source.ref` that `stage-ig-sites` clones from), `releases.json` from the repository's GitHub releases (a failed read writes nothing, never an empty list), `package.tgz` from the AST's resources, and the JSON-LD contexts the IG publishes. The first step of process `ig-docs-site-compose`.

root.description: The checkout whose IG instances are indexed. Default: the current directory's checkout.

work.description: Scratch directory for each IG's clone and restored AST. Default: a fresh temporary directory.

plan.description: Write nothing; say which instances would be indexed, and why any is skipped.

indexes.description: IG instances indexed; each skipped instance is named with its reason, never silently absent.

x-selection.when: Building the docs site or a staging preview, before any page step reads an IG instance's artefact index.
x-selection.limits: Needs the IG repository's AST cache branch: an IG with none is skipped, and the index is only as current as that cache (`ig-ast-cache`).
x-selection.cost: A shallow clone and an AST restore per IG, then seconds of indexing.

post.summary: Scan every page of a built IG site in a headless browser for markup shown as text
post.description: The checkout script `ig-site:page-render-qa`, the IG site build's last final step: it serves the built site locally, opens the root pages and the artefact pages (not the JSON views, mappings views or redirect stubs) in headless Chromium, waits for each to draw, and lists every text block that shows markdown as text (bold, list markers, links, images, code, headings, tables, HTML tags), code and preformatted text left out. It writes `assets/fhir-qa/page-render.json` and the script the QA report's "Page scan" panel draws it with. It reports and never fails the build: without a browser it writes why.

site.description: The built site directory.

limit.description: Scan at most this many pages.

concurrency.description: Pages open at once; 4 by default.

findings.description: Text blocks that show markup as text.

x-selection.when: After an IG site is built, so the QA report shows what its pages show a reader.
x-selection.limits: Needs Playwright and Chromium; without them it records why and scans nothing. Pages that do not finish drawing in 15 s are listed as unfinished.
x-selection.cost: About 20 s for 200 pages.

post.summary: Generate an IG instance's reader-facing pages from its artefact index
post.description: Write `<instance>/docs/` — an index page, one page per artefact, a page per over-large category and per menu group — from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` (and `menu.json` when ingested), styled by the template chrome an owning instance ingested. For an instance whose docs declare `igSite` it writes no index, menu or category pages — the IG site's own replace them — and only a front-matter `artifacts.md` naming the Tool that drew it. `build-ig-site` renders an IG's narrative pages from source; this Tool writes the artefact pages for every IG instance (`stage-ig-sites` copies them in).

instance.description: The instance directory: holds `fhir-artifact-index/` and receives `docs/`.

site.description: Where an instance declares a visualiser `renderedBy: ig-pages`, the Tool writes that visualiser's route page. With this site directory it writes ONLY those route pages (`<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, per instance, `…/<instance>/`) under it: not `docs/`, not the instance. Each opens the IG's artefact index.

label.description: The IG's display name. The index carries only the package id, which stands in when this is absent.

chrome-owner.description: The instance whose `chrome.json` styles the pages. Absent, the pages are unstyled and the build says so. The banner's identity is always the index's; a chrome ingested from another IG lends its tokens, never its status.

summary.description: Open the index page with the instance's own declaration (`harness_details.html` with `instance=`), making it the instance's landing page.

full-pages.description: Default: each artefact page is a thin shell at the same address, with its JSON-LD node, the index node (`artifact/index.jsonld`) and the shared renderer `assets/ig-artifact.js`. With it: full pages, no JSON-LD.

jsonld-base.description: Thin pages only: the docs root's published URL, so each node's IRIs are absolute. Absent, they are relative to the node's own file.

compiled-data.description: Where a compiled index's resource files are served, as a path from the docs root. `.` means each is served once at the docs root as `<Type>-<id>.json`, as the IG site does; a docs root beside the AST passes `../ast-data`.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when any page is stale or orphaned.

pages.description: Pages written; the menu and chrome are reported as present or COULD NOT DETERMINE, never silently absent.

x-selection.when: Building the docs site or a staging preview: an IG instance needs its artefact pages.
x-selection.limits: Narrative pages are not held — the harvest keeps artefacts — so menu entries link upstream. Bodies are still partly HTML inside markdown.
x-selection.cost: Seconds; one file per artefact.

post.summary: Put the IG Publisher's QA messages in each language an IG translates into, from the Publisher's own translations first
post.description: Fetches the IG Publisher's own message bundles (`Messages_<lang>.properties` in `org.hl7.fhir.utilities-<core>.jar`, Maven Central) at exactly the core version the AST recorded, and translates each QA message by its `message-id`: the Publisher's translation where it has one whose placeholders match the English, else this layer's catalogue `translations/<locale>/publisher/messages.po` (machine translation, marked as such), else the English. `needs --merge` appends to each locale's catalogue the strings a build lacks, each with an example and deep links to the rows that print it. The site build (`ig-qa-page.ts`) calls it for every locale the IG translates its pages into and publishes `qa-messages.<locale>.json` and `i18n-usage.json` beside the QA report.

merge.description: With `needs`: append what each locale lacks to its catalogue.

site.description: With `needs`: the published site's URL, so a catalogue's links open the rendered rows.

needs.description: Strings each locale lacks a translation for.

x-selection.when: When an IG's QA report is built for its translated locales, or to see and fill what a locale's catalogue lacks.
x-selection.limits: Needs curl and unzip and Maven Central for the bundles; without them every message falls back to this layer's catalogue or English, and the build says why. Never substitutes another core version.
x-selection.cost: One jar download (about 3 MB) per core version, cached under ~/.fhir/publisher-i18n.

post.summary: Cut an IG release as a GitHub draft that carries its packages and AST, and report a version left untagged or unreleased
post.description: Gather a release's files from a full Publisher build (package.tgz and its R4/R4B variants, and ast-data.zip, the IG's AST with the Libraries' ELM), say from sushi-config.yaml whether it is a pre-release, and make or refresh the GitHub DRAFT release for the tag with the files uploaded. The owner publishes the draft; a published release is never changed. `check` is the catch-up the AST refresh of the default branch runs (advisory): it reports a current version with no `v<version>` tag, naming the commit that set it for the owner to tag, and a tag with no release, for the owner to run `ig-release.yml` by hand. It never tags and never releases: the tag is the owner's governance step (`ig-release.bpmn`).

tag.description: `draft`: the git tag the release is for.

ig.description: `kind`, `check`: the IG root (its sushi-config.yaml and git history).

repo.description: `draft`, `check`: the repository (`owner/repo`) whose releases are read or written.

release.description: The files with size and SHA-256 (`assets`), `prerelease`/`release` (`kind`), what was done (`draft`), or what the owner should do (`check`).

x-selection.when: When the owner tags an IG version: the IG's `ig-release.yml` caller runs it after a full AST build of the tag. `check` runs in every AST refresh of the default branch.
x-selection.limits: Makes drafts only; publishing is the owner's step on GitHub. Needs a token that may write the repository's releases.
x-selection.cost: One full Publisher build (in the workflow), then a few REST calls and the uploads.

post.summary: Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration
post.description: The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (`index.config.json`): `ig-site:ast` restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (`ig-cache.sh restore`) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with `SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0`, and never accepted for the root); `ig-site:compose` derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in `$SITE_WORK/ig-api/`), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's `input/` and `sushi-config.yaml` (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; `ig-site:publisher-pages` serves each of the AST's resources once, as `<Type>-<id>.json` at the root (no `ast-data/` mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with `SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0` — the artefact index (or `fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json`, pointing at the cache's copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps `folio-build.json`. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in `FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES`, so the site build reports the IG's own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them.

ig.description: The IG checkout; the current directory by default.

baseurl.description: `compose`: the site's base path; `FOLIO_SITE_BASEURL` from the site build when absent.

work.description: The site build's work directory (`SITE_WORK` when absent): where `ast` writes its verdict, a layer above leaves the IG API sidecars, and `compose` the index `publisher-pages` serves.

pages.description: Pages composed, or AST files served.

x-selection.when: Publishing an IG repository's own site, as `stage-local.ts` does for a harnessed IG repository.
x-selection.limits: Needs the IG's AST cache branch (`ig-ast-refresh.yml` writes it) and the network to fetch it; asks the IG's origin for its default branch for edit links (absent, pages carry none). Never runs the Publisher.
x-selection.cost: Seconds to restore and compose; serving the AST is proportional to its size.

post.summary: Populate site.data.fhir for a just-the-docs IG render
post.description: Write the IG Publisher's Jekyll variables (`site.data.fhir.ig.*`, `packageId`, `canonical`) for ONE implementation guide, from `sushi-config.yaml` or a published IG's `fhir-artifact-index`, so pages written for the Publisher render on just-the-docs unchanged. fhir-harness declares `site.data` as a pass-through Liquid prefix; this is what Jekyll then reads.

ig.description: The IG root: holds `sushi-config.yaml`, or `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` for a published IG.

out.description: `<site>/_data/fhir.json` — Jekyll has one `_data/`, so one IG per site, as under the Publisher.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when the file is stale.

written.description: Fields written, each from a named source.

undetermined.description: Fields a Publisher build would have that no source here carries. LISTED, never written as empty strings, because Jekyll prints an empty string and an absent value identically.

x-selection.when: Rendering an IG's pages through just-the-docs instead of, or beside, the IG Publisher (`ig-publisher-reduction` P0).
x-selection.limits: Only the ImplementationGuide resource's fields plus `packageId` and `canonical`; no fuller Publisher schema is available to copy. A source describing a different package is refused, not merged.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds; reads two files.

post.summary: Run the immunization schedule-check app locally on a WHO or country IG
post.description: Start litlfred/awho-mcp's schedule-check web form on this machine: a HAPI FHIR server in Docker, the WHO SMART Immunizations IG loaded, then optionally a country adaptation IG (its decision-logic tables replace WHO's; its country profile is generated from its `input/l2/dependencies.yaml`), the CQL cache warmed, and the form served. Both listen on 127.0.0.1. Unbuilt IGs are built with SUSHI first, and each Library's CQL is embedded from `input/cql/` as the IG Publisher would. A re-run reuses a server loaded from the same commits; `--down` stops both.

who-ig.description: A WHO SMART Immunizations IG checkout, relative to the working directory (the folder holding the checkouts, e.g. `~/space_cats`).

country-ig.description: A country adaptation IG checkout, e.g. `smart-immunizations-uganda`, relative to the working directory. Without it the app follows WHO's own schedule.

down.description: Stop the form and the server.

url.description: The form on 127.0.0.1. It stores nothing; each check is one inline `$apply` round.

x-install.cli: git clone https://github.com/litlfred/awho-mcp && cd awho-mcp && python3 -m pip install -e .

x-selection.when: Trying or demonstrating the immunizations L4 app on a clean IG build, before anything is hosted, on the viewer's own machine.
x-selection.limits: Immunizations only (awho-mcp's catalog is the WHO SMART Immunizations IG). One country per server, because a country IG reuses WHO's PlanDefinition ids. Local only: nothing is published and the URL does not open from another machine.
x-selection.cost: Docker and about 4 GB of memory. First run: the HAPI image pull, about a minute to load and warm, and a SUSHI build of any unbuilt IG. A re-run on the same commits restarts only the form.

post.summary: Convert a checkout to a root index.config.json
post.description: Write the root `index.config.json` (`folio-index-config/v1`) that says which layers the checkout instantiates, where each comes from (`source.local` or `source.remote`) and which owns `/` (`site.landing`), from the root `*.config.json` files and the declaration's `remoteMounts`. With `--write` it moves `remoteMounts` off the declaration into `source.remote` entries, writes the generated `.gitignore` block, and renames a legacy `<name>.mount-lock.json` to `index.lock.json`. Without a flag it prints the index it would write. Idempotent: a re-run merges what the declaration gained, and refuses an entry the index already holds differently. A root config naming no layer is reported as `unmatched-config` and not imported, because what to do with it is a person's decision.

root.description: The checkout to convert; omitted, this one.

write.description: Write the index, move the mounts, write the ignore block and rename the lock.

check.description: Exit 1 when --write would change anything; write nothing.

findings.description: The index it would write or wrote, and each finding (`unmatched-config`, `unreadable-config`, `landing-undetermined`). Exit 0 written, up to date or planned; 1 stale under --check; 2 could not convert.

post.summary: Ingest, with PDF and image extensions
post.description: Ingest a PDF into `library/` — embedded outline, page text, OCR for scans, and image extraction — using PyMuPDF, tesseract and pypdf with Pillow.

file.description: The PDF to ingest, under the declared `uploads` graph.

x-selection.when: Reach for this when the upload is a PDF and you need its CONTENT — an outline-bearing document read at chapter granularity, a text-layer document read at page granularity, or a scan that must be OCR'd first. Confirm the backend is present before relying on it: `bun run cat check-deps`, or simply run the pair's entry point, which reports `no PDF backend` rather than guessing.
x-selection.limits: It adds nothing for archives, spreadsheets or metadata — `ingest-stdlib` does those, and does them where this cannot run. Its PDF rungs are tested in CI, which installs the lean set; the table rung (`pdf-tables.py`, camelot) is not, so anything gated on it is a path CI cannot exercise.

The dependencies are not independent either: `pypdf` image extraction needs `Pillow`, and `cryptography` panics under pyo3 on IMPORT when `cffi` is missing. All of it is declared in `schemas/sdlc/python-deps.ts`, so the cost is read rather than rediscovered.

post.summary: Ingest an IG's navigation from its sushi-config
post.description: Read `menu:` (and the page tree) out of an IG source repository's `sushi-config.yaml` into `fhir-artifact-index/menu.json`, recording the repository and commit it was read at — the declared source `stage-ig-sites` clones. `--check` re-derives it against a checkout; with no `--source` it reports COULD NOT DETERMINE and exits 2, never 0.

source.description: A checkout of the IG source repository.

out.description: The instance's `fhir-artifact-index/` directory.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when stale, 2 when it cannot compare.

groups.description: Menu groups read, each with its items.

x-selection.when: An IG instance gains, or re-pins, the source repository its site is built from.
x-selection.limits: Reads the config only: a menu item the Publisher generates (a page with no source) is listed, and the site build reports it.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds.

post.summary: Record an IG's GitHub releases as pointers to their binary assets
post.description: Read an IG repository's GitHub releases and write `fhir-artifact-index/releases.json` (`ig-releases/v1`): each asset's name, size, SHA-256 digest and download URL, never its bytes. The IG site's generated `releases` page lists them.

repo.description: `owner/repo`; default the instance menu's recorded IG source, else its declaration's `repository`.

x-selection.when: After an IG repository cuts a release, so its pages list the new assets.
x-selection.limits: A record of what GitHub reported on the day it was read; a later release is absent until the next run. Drafts are never recorded.

post.description: Ingest an upload into `library/` using only the Python standard library — archive listings, CSV and spreadsheet records, technical file metadata, and the content sniff that routes a file to its rung.

post.summary: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
post.description: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness's declaration at its pin and every `needs`, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless --repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch's tip unless --pin says otherwise, its declaration's name checked), seeds them all into the repository's index.config.json with the consent given (`remote-mount --seed --whole`), sets `site.landing` to the harness, `site.agentRun` and `mountApprovers`, mounts the closure (`remote-mount`: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (`.github/cat.ts` and `.github/mount-from-lock.sh` from cat-harness-tools `templates/root-bootstrap/`) and sets the root's `cat` script to `bun .github/cat.ts`, so `bun run cat …` mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness's `instantiate:<harness>` checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/<harness>). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:<harness>` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches/<branch>/ (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin <name>=<sha>` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of <name>=<owner/repo>` says where a need lives.

branch.description: The setup branch. Default: harness/<harness>. Never the default branch.

local.description: Commit on the branch, push nothing; the site is built and composed (stage-local --dry-run).

noPr.description: Push the branch and the preview, open no PR.

x-selection.limits: The harness's own adoption steps are its checkout scripts instantiate:<harness> and prepare:<harness>; a harness that declares neither is mounted and rendered with what its layers already declare, and a site that needs a build input nobody produced (an IG with no AST) is refused by the render step with its reason. Re-pinning an already harnessed repository is remote-mount --seed, not this.
x-selection.cost: The mount: a blobless fetch of each layer of the closure and one install (a few minutes). Then the harness's prepare step (an IG's AST: a full IG Publisher run) and the render.

post.summary: Every reference a journey or a workshop names resolves
post.description: Read every `user-scenario` and `workshop` node in the checkout through the layers' declared directories, with the journeys viewer's own resolver, and resolve what each names: actors (`personas`, a step's `lead`, `experiences[].actor`, `handoff.from`/`to`, `illustrationStyle.cast[].actor`), user stories, `realisedBy` BPMN files (instance-relative) and the element ids in them, `uses` blocks in a directory declaring `building-blocks`, `req:` requirements, FHIR examples and a step's `dak` assets (data sets, decision tables, indicators) in a `fhir-artifact-index` (could not determine while the index is built at publish), `illustration.src` files, `follows`/`partOf`/`parts`/`includes` journeys (parts and includes forming no cycle; an `includes` held against the call activity its step's `realisedBy` names, could not determine when the call names no process), the `trustLadder` code list and each `record.state` code of it, and ArchiMate `views`; and each workshop's `scenarios`, `steps[]` `{scenario, step}` and `<scenario>#<step>` refs; each device screen's `owner` and `personCard` actors, its `steps[]` `{scenario, step}`, and the FHIR examples its `qr` and `recordList` blocks name; and every persona's `avatar` image path. Every journey is a DAK user scenario (the kind `specialises` it): its DAK personas, the roles its persona actors play, must be non-empty and each a declared role; a persona may be an actor or (0.4.0) a role. What is derived is not also written: a listed part's `follows` or `partOf`, personas equal to the parts', a lead equal to the lanes' first actor, are each a redundant finding, and a 0.4.0 step with no experiences whose lanes no persona plays is a finding. A node that does not parse is a finding. One line per finding, naming the layer, file and step. Exit 0 every reference resolves (or no layer holds a journey or a workshop, which is said); 1 one does not; 2 the declarations could not be read.

root.description: A directory in the checkout to check. Default: the working directory.

json.description: Print the report as JSON.

findings.description: Unresolved references and unparsed nodes, one line each on stderr, with the count of references examined; or one ✓ line.

x-selection.when: In every layer pull request's checks (it is a `check:` script, so the gate set derives it), and before publishing a site whose layer declares a `journeys-viewer` visualiser: a journey that names a story, a BPMN task, a block or an image that is not there.
x-selection.limits: A `realisedBy` process and an `illustration.src` are resolved in the journey's own layer only, as the viewer draws them; the other references are looked up in the journey's layer first, then in every layer the checkout mounts.
x-selection.cost: One read of the checkout's declared directories, as the viewer makes; milliseconds per journey.

post.description: Draw every journey (`user-scenario`) and workshop (`workshop`) in the checkout as static pages at the route of the visualiser a layer declares for this Tool, `<locale>/<instance>/<id>/`: an index of all journeys, grouped by layer (each a sub-graph page), each parent's `parts` nested under it in its order with optional and repeating parts marked (an older file's `partOf` children after them, ordered along `follows`), and a plain DAK user scenario with no steps listed as one; one page per journey, its parts in order and the journeys it is a part of, a journey map with a lane and a feeling curve per persona, then each step, linked to the journey it `includes`, with its BPMN drawing (the step's flow nodes highlighted), user stories, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks, the DAK assets it uses (data sets, decision tables and indicators, linked into the IG) and ArchiMate views; and the workshop layer, the questions for the room on each step, a page per workshop and per module, job aids, and printable A3/A4 sheets; and each device screen (`device-screen`) that shows a step a workshop presents, drawn as a static device mock (phone, tablet, scanner, desktop, kiosk) with its owner beside it, in the workshop's Device Demo, linked both ways with the walkthrough. A persona's picture (`meta.persona.avatar`) is drawn wherever the persona appears. Layers below the declaring one are read through their declarations, so a downstream site shows the journeys of the layers it mounts too.

site.description: A site being built: the pages are written at the declared route under it. Absent, under the layer's own site directory. The route is this Tool's alone and is replaced whole.

pages.description: The viewer's pages and its two assets (`assets/journeys.css`, `assets/journeys.js`), under the declared route.

x-selection.when: A site build of a layer that declares a `journeys-viewer` visualiser over its `user-scenario`, `workshop` and `device-screen` directories; run with the other declared writers (`visualiser-writers.ts`), before the navbar pass.
x-selection.limits: Static pages: the stepper, the filter and the remembered assessment ticks are a small dependency-free script, and every page reads complete without it. A FHIR example links to its page only where a layer declares a `fhir-artifact-index`; an ArchiMate view is drawn only where its layer declares `archimate-pages`. A device screen is drawn in the one state its node says: a toggle is drawn on or off, a button is a label; a workshop that declares no screen for its steps frames its own app (`presentation.deviceDemo`) instead.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per journey; a BPMN drawing is inlined once per step that names it.

post.summary: Judge a tree and record the verdict by digest
post.description: Run the layer PR-check gates and tests on a composed tree (head) and on its base, or reuse a stored verdict whose digest is the base tree's, compare them with the layer-pr-checks compare scripts, and write a verdict record: {treeDigest, runner {kind agent|github-actions|local, id}, startedAt, finishedAt, gates [{name, exit, seconds, skipped?}], tests {total, failed, new}, verdict green|red|unknown}. With a token it publishes the verdict as the commit status `judge-tree`; `check` answers whether any runner judged a digest green; `sample` re-runs a seeded few gates of a record.

lock.description: The index.lock.json whose fixity digests name every layer but the caller.

caller.description: The caller as owner/name (or its lock layer): the entry replaced by its PR tree. Every runner must name it the same way.

caller-dir.description: The caller's git checkout; its HEAD^{tree} (or --sha's) is the PR tree.

sha.description: The head commit: whose tree is read from --caller-dir, and where the status is published.

root.description: The mounted index with the caller swapped in, where run-gates.py runs.

instance.description: The own layer(s) run-gates.py judges; repeatable.

base-verdict.description: A stored verdict record standing in for the base run; refused unless its treeDigest is the base tree's (--base-tree).

base-root.description: A mounted base tree to run the gates on instead.

test-path.description: What `bun test` runs on each side; none means no tests.

publish.description: Post the commit status `judge-tree` when GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN is set; without one, the record file is the verdict.

record.description: The verdict record, `<records-dir>/<treeDigest>.json` unless --out names it; valid against the tools layer's `schemas/verdict-record.schema.json`. Three exit codes: 0 green, 1 red, 2 COULD NOT DETERMINE (no judging scripts, a stored base verdict for another tree, a compare script that crashed, or no gate ran). 2 is never green, and neither is a verdict for another digest.

x-selection.when: When a PR's tree must be judged and any runner can do it: an agent before pushing, a developer locally, or CI. Then `verdict-check.yml` passes the PR on the published verdict instead of re-running ~300 gates per side.
x-selection.limits: The digest trusts the lock's fixity digests for every layer but the caller, so a run that takes lower layers at main instead of the lock judges a tree the digest does not name. A verdict answers only for its exact digest: a change to the judging scripts is a new digest and needs a new verdict.
x-selection.cost: That of layer-pr-checks for one side, or two when no stored base verdict exists: gates dominate (minutes to tens of minutes). `digest` and `check` are one hash and at most one HTTP request.

strict.description: Promote `major` to failing as well. Not what CI runs; see the note on constant-red checks in `remote-skill-servable.test.ts`.

sidecars.description: The QA tree, mirroring each subject's own path, because a flat tree would collide: several basenames occur twice.

worstSeverity.description: critical, major, minor — or none. `unknown` findings are never a pass.

post.description: Extract the interior of one BPMN file as the L2-BPMN subgraph (`smart-base/L2-bpmn/schemas/extract-bpmn.ts`, ported from WHO smart-kg `tools/extract-bpmn.mjs`): a `bpmn-definitions` node and its processes, participants, tasks, gateways, events, the `flowsTo`/`messageTo`/`contains` edges between them, and one `performedBy` edge from each pool to the persona its @name matches against the ActorDefinition titles under `--personas`. The output is a graph document whose `@context` is the l2-bpmn context and validates with the engine's `check()`.

personas.description: A directory of ActorDefinition FSH; a pool's @name is matched against their titles. When absent, every pool -> persona join is recorded unresolved.

out.description: Where the graph document goes; stdout when absent.

graph.description: The L2-BPMN graph document (nodes, edges, provenance).

x-selection.when: A BPMN file's interior is to be read into the knowledge graph as the L2-BPMN subgraph, with its pool -> persona joins recorded and their resolution status made queryable.
x-selection.limits: Parses the OMG BPMN serialisation with regular expressions, as smart-kg did; it reads tasks, sub-processes, exclusive gateways, start/end events, sequence and message flows, and does not interpret diagram layout. A pool -> persona match is exact string equality on a display title, so it does not survive a rename.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network.

post.description: Extract the L1 citations from a DMN decision table's reference column (`smart-base/L2-dmn/schemas/extract-citations.ts`, ported from WHO smart-kg `tools/extract-citations.mjs`): one `external-artifact` node for the table and one `citation` node per distinct reference string, each left `unresolved`, with `appearsIn` edges and a coverage report of how many rules cite an L1 source. A citation string is content-addressed in the DAK's namespace, so the same string is one node here and in the L2-DMN graph's `citesSource` edges. The output is an L2 document.

out.description: Where the graph document goes; also echoed to stdout when absent.

graph.description: The citation graph document (an L2 document: the table as an external artefact and its L1 citation nodes), plus a coverage report on stderr.

x-selection.when: A DMN decision table carries an L1 reference column and its citations are to be turned into graph nodes, with coverage counted rather than assumed.
x-selection.limits: Copies each reference string verbatim and never resolves it to a publication — resolution is a judgement the schema requires evidence for. '[Add appropriate reference]' is recorded as a placeholder, which coverage counts apart from a blank. The reference column is found by its description.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network.

post.summary: dak.json + FSH tree → L2 DAK component graph
post.description: Extract the DAK component layer (L2) from a smart-base-shaped IG (`smart-base/L2/schemas/extract-dak.ts`, ported from WHO smart-kg `tools/extract-dak.mjs`): a `dak` node from dak.json, a `persona` node per ActorDefinition, a `functional`/`non-functional-requirement` node per requirement instance with its `requirement-statement`s, the `hasComponent`/`hasStatement` edges, and the `fulfilledBy` edges that resolve each requirement's `actor = Canonical(...)` against a persona's instance id. Coverage is reported across all nine DAK components, including the empty ones, and files present with no component declaring them are listed. Distinct from the existing `extract-dak` tool (WHO's spreadsheet extractor).

dak.description: The dak.json with the kit's metadata (canonicalUrl, title, version).

bpmnDir.description: A BPMN directory; its files are listed as business-process orphans when no component declares them.

dmnDir.description: A DMN directory; its files are listed as decision-logic orphans when no component declares them.

out.description: Where the graph document goes; stdout when absent.

graph.description: The L2 DAK component graph document, with coverage across all nine components on stderr.

x-selection.when: A DAK's component layer is to be read into the knowledge graph from dak.json and the committed FSH instances, with the gaps (components with no instance, files no component declares) made visible.
x-selection.limits: Reads the FSH instance tree, not the DAK spreadsheets; it covers personas and requirements, the components the estate commits as instances. Kit membership is inferred from presence in the input tree, since dak.json declares no component arrays. The `fulfilledBy` join resolves by canonical reference and does not depend on a display title.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network.

post.description: Extract the interior of one DMN decision table as the L2-DMN subgraph (`smart-base/L2-dmn/schemas/extract-dmn.ts`, ported from WHO smart-kg `tools/extract-dmn.mjs`): a `dmn-definitions` node and its decisions, decision tables, input and output clauses and rules, the `reads` edges to the data elements recovered from input expressions, the `citesSource` edges to the L1 citations each rule's reference column names, and the `invokedBy` edge to the BPMN task the `usingTask` href names. Pass `--bpmn` to resolve that task by name instead of recording it unresolved.

bpmn.description: A BPMN file; the `usingTask` href fragment is matched against its task @name to resolve `invokedBy`.

out.description: Where the graph document goes; stdout when absent.

graph.description: The L2-DMN graph document. Its `citesSource` edges reach L1 citations minted by kg-extract-citations from the same strings.

x-selection.when: A DMN decision table's interior is to be read into the knowledge graph as the L2-DMN subgraph, joining its rules to the L1 sources they cite and to the BPMN task that invokes the decision.
x-selection.limits: Parses the DMN serialisation with regular expressions, as smart-kg did. A data element recovered from an input expression carries only the name that was referenced, never a definition, and is left unresolved. The reference column is found by its description, and the outputEntry/annotationEntry split is read from the first rule.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network.

post.description: Extract the L3 index from a SMART Guidelines IG's source tree (`smart-base/L3/schemas/extract-l3.ts`, ported from WHO smart-kg `tools/extract-l3.mjs`): one thin node per FHIR artefact (PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, Library, Measure, Questionnaire, StructureMap/Definition, ValueSet, CodeSystem, ConceptMap, ActorDefinition, Requirements, CQL) read from FSH, FML and JSON with RuleSets expanded, the real `uses` and `citesSource` canonical references, and the `implementedBy` edges that tie each artefact to the L2 component its Title names by the SOP's id convention. Coverage is reported across every artefact type.

out.description: Where the graph document goes; stdout when absent.

graph.description: The L3 graph document; each node carries the SHA-256 of the file it came from.

x-selection.when: A built or source IG's FHIR artefacts are to be indexed as the L3 subgraph and tied back to the L2 components and L1 recommendations they implement.
x-selection.limits: Reads the FSH/FML/JSON source, not a built package; the L2 joins are the SOP's Title-and-id conventions (no back-pointer extension exists), so they are recorded unresolved with the rule that matched them. Only artefact types with committed instances are modelled; ExampleScenario, TestPlan and TestScript are reported absent.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network.

post.description: Retrieve and inspect a remote Knowledge Graph packaged as an npm package or tarball (.tgz), supporting both unhydrated source graph views (authored declarations, skills, schemas) and hydrated materialized graph views (subgraph JSON-LD, metadata indexes, dereferenced graph projections).

post.summary: Validate a node in the graph
post.description: Check one file against the schema for its graph typology. ONE tool for every schema: the kind is resolved from the declared directory that holds the file.

path.description: The node to check. Its graph typology is resolved from the declared directory that contains it.

lenient.description: Accept partial coverage knowingly: downgrade could-not-determine from an error to a warning.

report.description: One line per file — valid, invalid with the failing paths, or could-not-determine with the reason. Exit 0 valid, 1 invalid or undetermined, 2 misuse.

x-selection.when: Whenever a node's shape matters and you are not in this repository's CI: `tools/` is an INHERITED declaration and `.github/workflows/` is not, so a downstream layer gets this and none of the CI gates.

post.description: Render the layer's published knowledge graph as one page: facets by kind and sub-graph, search, a node's properties, its edges and back-links, and the graph's own gaps — reading the JSON-LD document at the site root rather than carrying a copy.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.description: Is a `library/<bib-slug>/` entry complete as L1 source content? Each requirement is met, unmet, or NOT-DERIVABLE.

targetPath.description: One `library/<bib-slug>/` entry. Absent, every entry the declared `library` graph holds.

report.description: Per requirement: met, unmet, or `not-derivable` — the third distinguishes a document that CANNOT yield an artefact from one that simply has not. Exit 2 means no `library` graph is declared anywhere, which the script states as "This is NOT a pass. Treat it as unknown."

post.description: Of the normative sentences in a publication (the closed marker list of the methodology `l1-coverage` §1), count how many an L1 extraction CAPTURED, how many are EXCLUDED for a fixed-list reason a person signed off, and how many are UNACCOUNTED — per page and in total. Writes the contract's §4 report and exits non-zero below 100% accounted-for.

text.description: The publication's body text, page-tagged: `{"pages":[{"page":n,"text":"…"}]}` JSON, or plain text with a form feed between pages (what `pdftotext` writes). Headers, references and tables of contents are stripped by the caller.

captured.description: JSON `[{"id","text"}]`: every statement the extraction captured, verbatim.

exclusions.description: JSON `[{location|text, reason, signedOffBy?, signedOffAt?}]`. An exclusion without `signedOffBy` is a proposal and leaves its sentence unaccounted.

out.description: Where to write the report; stdout when absent.

report.description: An `l1-coverage-report/v1` JSON report: definitionVersion, matchMethod, source and graph sha256, totals, pages[] and sentences[]. A per-page table goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: An L1 extraction of a publication (recommendations, remarks, schedule entries) is about to be reviewed or promoted, and somebody needs to know — rather than assume — that no normative sentence was silently missed.
x-selection.limits: Matching is normalised substring, so a paraphrased capture reads as unaccounted. Body-text filtering is the caller's. The marker list is English.
x-selection.cost: Reads three files; no network.

post.summary: L1 extraction viewer: a hub and a page per instance with `l1-extraction` directories
post.description: For every visualiser an instance declares with `renderedBy: l1-extraction-pages`, write the hub at `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, with `subgraphs: "instance"`, one page per instance that declares an `l1-extraction` directory. Each page shows, from what the files declare: the L1 statements (graph nodes with a `statement`, and an authored L1 source's `recommendations`); the candidate work list's counts, coverage and decisions; each graph document's nodes by type and edges by predicate (L2 scenario candidates included); counts of curation, mapping, vocabulary, exclusions and run context; and a link from every file to its published copy (cat-harness's `library:viz`), when the site has it, and to its source at the pinned commit. A declared directory not on disk is reported UNKNOWN, never zero.

site.description: The site being built; pages go under it (cat-harness-tools' `visualiser-writers.ts` passes it). Default: the checkout's site directory.

root.description: The checkout whose declarations are read. Default: the checkout holding the working directory.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a page is stale, missing or orphaned.

pages.description: Pages written: the hub and one per instance.

x-selection.when: Publishing a site that should show what each L1 extraction holds.
x-selection.limits: Validates nothing (`l1-recommendation-candidates` and `l1-recommendation-scenarios` do, on every write) and does not re-render the JSON-LD (the library viewer publishes it).
x-selection.cost: Reads each file of each declared directory once.

post.description: Find every normative sentence of an ingested `library/` entry (folio-assistant-core's `l1-coverage` markers), flag uncertain readings, and propose the publication's identity. Given an agent's `l1-recommendation-curation/v1`, refuse a non-verbatim statement or an unknown location, and write the recommendations and remarks as an L1 3.0 graph (checked with `L1/schemas/validate.ts`) with coverage and proposed, unsigned exclusions.

curation.description: The agent's decisions per candidate location (`l1-recommendation-curation/v1`). Absent: only the work list is written.

candidates.description: `recommendation-candidates.json` — every normative sentence, its hints and its decision; cites the run context.

graph.description: `l1.json` — L1 3.0 publication, recommendation and remark nodes, every one `inferred`.

exclusions.description: `exclusions.proposed.json`, in `l1-coverage`'s shape; none counts until a person signs it.

post.summary: Publish the dynamic Lean viewer: doc-gen4 declaration data as knowledge-graph shards

post.summary: What this layer's MCP server serves
post.description: Read the real tool surface from the registrars by mounting each against a capture object — the same objects the server asks, so the Zod shapes and their optionality are the served ones rather than a reading of the source.

Three exit codes: 0 the surface was captured whole, 2 one or more modules COULD NOT BE READ so the capture is incomplete, and no equivalence verdict may be drawn from it. post.summary: Merge leftover (has a PR's intent landed?)
post.description: After a train merged, compare a PR's head with the base path by path and say whether what it still changes is ONLY generated files, generated README regions, or changes the base already carries (its patch applies in reverse to the base): `landed`, `not-landed` with the authored paths still different, or `could-not-determine`, which is never shown as clean. Only reports; closing the PR stays a steward action.

member.description: The PR number or branch. On the command line a PR may be pinned as `N:<sha>`.

base.description: The base the train landed on; default `origin/main`.

report.description: `merge-leftover/v1` on stdout. Exit 0 landed, 1 not-landed, 2 could not determine.

x-selection.when: After a train lands, for each member PR still open, before the steward decides whether to close it.
x-selection.limits: An authored path whose lines the base rewrote after the train reads `not-landed`: the reverse patch no longer applies, and only a person can say whether the rewrite kept the intent.
x-selection.cost: One fetch, then one `git diff` and one `git apply --check` per authored path, in a throwaway index. No working tree is touched.

post.description: For the open PRs (via `gh`, or a list of branches), report which pairs would conflict: pairwise overlap on AUTHORED paths, with generated paths excluded using the merge-conflict-patterns declaration; which PRs touch a shared declaration (a layer's `<instance>.json`, `roles.json`, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, schemas, BPMN/DMN); and which touch the harness layer's directory or its tools layer's. A PR that could not be measured makes no pair independent. JSON (`merge-overlap/v1`), the conflict-prediction input for composing trains.

base.description: The base each PR is diffed against from its fork point; default `origin/main`.

branches.description: Branches to compare instead of the open PRs; with none, the open PRs come from `gh`.

report.description: `merge-overlap/v1` on stdout: per member `authored_paths`, `region_paths`, `touches_shared`, the two harness flags; every pair that is not independent, with why.

x-selection.when: Before composing a merge train, and whenever deciding which PRs can land together or must be ordered.
x-selection.limits: Paths, not semantics: two PRs that change different files can still interact, which the shared-declaration list only partly covers. A README counts as authored when its prose changed, as a region when only generated regions did.
x-selection.cost: One REST listing (`gh api …/pulls`; not `gh pr list`, which is GraphQL) and one `git fetch` of every open head, then a `git diff --name-only` per PR. No working tree is touched.

post.description: Build a train branch from a base SHA: merge each member (a PR number or branch) with `merge-base.ts --no-regen`, refusing — never hand-resolving — a member whose conflicts no declared pattern covers; then one `bun run cat regen`, `check:l1-complete --write`, every check a layer declares `afterMerge` (its declared writer run when red), and `kg:audit:all:check`; then merge `origin/main`, taking main's side of generated conflicts and regenerating once more. Emits a `merge-train-report/v1` JSON report. Never pushes, opens or merges a PR.

base.description: The commit the train branch starts from.

branch.description: The train branch to create; default `merge-train/<base>-<time>`.

dry-run.description: Simulate with `git merge-tree`: classify each member's conflicts against the simulated train and change nothing.

members.description: PR numbers or branches, in train order. On the command line a PR may be pinned to the head CI saw as `N:<sha>`.

report.description: `merge-train-report/v1` on stdout: members merged, refused with reasons and conflicted paths, the checks run, main's merge, and the head. Exit 0 built, 1 needs a person, 2 could not start.

x-selection.when: The steward has chosen a batch of green, mutually independent PRs (see merge-overlap) and wants one branch that carries them all, regenerated once.
x-selection.limits: Each member's merge commit is not proved on its own; the train is proved at its end by one regen. A refused member is left out and reported — handing it back to its owner is the steward's step. It does not push: CI on the train runs only after the steward pushes it.
x-selection.cost: One `merge-base.ts` per member (seconds each), then one regen (5-13 min) and the three checks; a second regen if main had generated conflicts.

post.summary: Validate draft MeSH headings against NLM's authority
post.description: Stage three of `skill-pipeline-subject-indexing` for MeSH: look up every candidate heading of a draft (a preferred heading, an entry term, or a descriptor id, with an optional qualifier) in NLM's MeSH authority at id.nlm.nih.gov, current year. Each candidate comes back `resolved` (in the preferred form), `qualifier-not-allowed` (descriptor kept, qualifier dropped), `ambiguous` (options listed for a person) or `not-found` (dropped). It never adds a heading the draft did not propose and never emits one the authority lacks.

draft.description: A JSON file: `{ "candidates": [{ "label"?, "descriptor"?, "qualifier"?, "why"? }] }`, in the order stage two ranked them.

json.description: Print the full report as JSON instead of the review table.

report.description: A review table with one row per candidate, or with `--json` the report: `results` per candidate and `validated`, the headings a reviewer sees.

x-selection.when: A draft list of MeSH headings from stages one and two of `mesh-subject-indexing` is ready to be checked against the authority.
x-selection.limits: Checks existence, preferred form and allowable qualifiers only. It does not judge whether a heading fits the work, and applies none of NLM's rules on heading count or major topics.
x-selection.cost: Two or three HTTPS requests per candidate to id.nlm.nih.gov; about a second for a short draft.

post.summary: Replay a committed mount lock with nothing but Node
post.description: Lay down every remote mount `index.lock.json` records — each layer fetched at the lock's full SHA (sparse, blob-filtered), each directory verified against its `treeDigest`, a mismatch undone and reported — importing only `node:*`, so it runs on a fresh clone before any layer is present. It never decides what to mount: `remote-mount` writes the lock (and checks trust); this only replays it. Refuses to write over a path with tracked files or bytes that no longer hash to the lock. Exit 0 mounted/current, 1 missing, 2 could-not-determine.

x-selection.limits: It lives in cat-harness, which is itself a mounted layer, so it cannot bootstrap a checkout that does not already hold cat-harness. The parent must carry its own dependency-free entry point that fetches this script at the pin (e.g. a `.github/mount-from-lock.sh`) — never call this path directly from a workflow in a repository that mounts cat-harness. A downstream root's `cat` script, `bun .github/cat.ts`, runs that entry point when the layers are missing, so `bun run cat <name>` works from `git clone`.
x-selection.cost: One shallow, blob-filtered fetch per locked layer; a few seconds each. `--check` needs no network.

Acting on a number is `bun run cat narratives:confirm <n>` or `bun run cat narratives:reject <n> --why <r>`, and both REFUSE outside a terminal: `reviewer()` throws with "Confirming is a PERSON's act; an agent running this would be recorded as one". The refusal is needed because `git config user.name` is the agent's, so an agent's confirmation would be recorded as a person's. So this node does not offer the confirming arms: an agent may read the queue and must not answer it. A rejection with no reason is refused too, not defaulted, because a reason-less rejection lets the next agent redraft the identical thing.
