commit.description: The commit the site was built from, named in the pages commit message (env COMMIT_SHA).

pagesDir.description: A git checkout whose `origin` holds the `gh-pages` branch (env PAGES_DIR).

result.description: `published on attempt <n>`, or `nothing to publish`; any other exit is a publish that did not happen.

x-selection.when: The deploy step of a site publish: after the site is built and checked, to replace the live `gh-pages` tree without dropping the previews on it.
x-selection.limits: A full replace of the whole branch. A branch preview (`branches/<branch>/`) is published by the staging route, which replaces only its own directory.
x-selection.cost: A shallow fetch, a copy of the site and a push, repeated on a lost race.

post.description: Run every registered criterion over the blocks under a path and write a per-block QA sidecar. A sidecar rather than a console report, because a printed verdict cannot distinguish "never checked" from "checked and clean".

targetPath.description: The content root to sweep. Absent, the command exits 2 with its usage — could-not-determine, not a clean sweep.

dryRun.description: Report what would change without writing sidecars.

ci.description: Fail on a finding rather than recording it.

sidecars.description: One `<block>.qa.json` per block, committed beside its subject.

post.summary: Give every page Jekyll did not lay out the folio-assistant navbar
post.description: A LAST pass over the finished site: inject the shared navbar (`lib/navbar.ts`, the same component the site sidebar draws) into every page that carries none — standalone viewers, generated layer pages, and each IG site built by `stage-ig-sites`. A page under an `igSite` layer's route is railed as THAT layer's page (its name, mark and graphs); a page may declare its own section (`data-fa-visualiser-nav`) and its label (`fa-visualiser-label`). Mount routes are left to the mount pass, and a page that declines (`folio-navbar: none`) is left bare.

site.description: The finished site directory.

built.description: The layer whose site this is (`cat-harness`).

foreign-site.description: The site is a folio's, not the platform's: platform links point at the platform's published site.

instance.description: With `--foreign-site`: the layer whose own site this is. Its name, mark and graphs head the navbar, and Harnesses lists it (linking to this site's root) and the harnesses it is built on.

railed.description: Pages given the navbar, beside those already navigated, redirect stubs, pages that declined, and pages with no <body> — each counted, none silently.

post.description: Verify every Markdown link in a folio's README still resolves — relative paths against the tree, repo refs against a real ls-tree, Pages URLs against the publish ref. Writes nothing.

file.description: The file to audit; the README by default.

dir.description: The folio root, when not the working directory.

findings.description: Resolved, dead, or NOT CHECKED — the third state is never rendered as either of the other two.

post.description: Rewrite each generated README region, and only where the README already carries that section's marker pair. Nothing outside a marked region is touched. The layer's AGENTS.md is synced too, for the `skills:index` index only: the skills the layer publishes, or, past 32 KiB, their directories with the full list in SKILLS.md.

check.description: Fail if any section is stale; write nothing.

only.description: Restrict to these sections. Repeated: the flag is emitted once per section.

report.description: Per section: written, unchanged, or skipped because it could not be determined.

post.description: Split each library entry's reference lists (a References, Bibliography or Further reading section or heading, in the six UN languages and Portuguese) into folio-reference/v1 nodes in the instance's declared `references` directory, one per cited work, keyed `<doc-id>.<section>.<n>`: provenance extracted, derivedFrom the section file, printed the entry verbatim, and only the fields read without guessing (URL, DOI, ISBN, year, access date). The bibliography page lists them as the document's own bibliography. `--check` writes nothing and fails when a node is stale.

instance.description: The instance root whose library sections are read and whose references directory is written.

entry.description: One library entry's slug, to extract only its lists.

check.description: Fail if a node is stale, instead of writing.

x-selection.when: A library entry's source prints a reference list and the document should have its own bibliography. For glossary and abbreviations sections use glossary-from-source.
x-selection.limits: Reads L1 sections, not the PDF; no title or author is parsed (the node keeps the printed text). Only nodes with provenance extracted are written or removed.
x-selection.cost: Seconds for a few hundred entries; reads sections, no network.

post.description: Rewrite each reference-list block of a document (a block whose `meta.referenceList` is set) from the folio-reference/v1 nodes its `cites` names, in that order: the node's `printed` text verbatim when it has one, otherwise WHO style (or the short `Authors. Title. Year.` form), as a numbered or bulleted list. The block's `.md` is generated whole. `--check` writes nothing and fails when a list is stale.

instance.description: The instance root whose folio blocks and references directories are read.

check.description: Fail if a list is stale, instead of writing.

blocks.description: The rewritten reference-list blocks: each block's `.md`.

x-selection.when: A document's References list should come from the reference nodes its block cites. For glossary or acronyms tables use glossary-table.
x-selection.limits: Only blocks with `meta.referenceList`; the whole `.md` is regenerated. A cited key with no reference node fails the run.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per block; reads the instance's blocks and reference nodes, no network.

post.description: Propose the next version of each package from conventional-commit messages, open a release PR with the CHANGELOG and version bump, and — when that PR is merged — create the tag and GitHub release. Does not publish to a registry. Declared here, not configured: no config file and no tag exist in this repository.

package.description: The package being released. release-please proposes every package it is configured for; this is the one whose tag is wanted.

repo.description: owner/name of the repository the release is made in; the current one when absent.

tag.description: The tag created when the release PR merges, `<package>-v<version>`.

x-install.cli: npm install -g release-please (or the GitHub Action googleapis/release-please-action@v4)

x-selection.when: A repository whose commits follow conventional-commit messages and that releases often enough that doing it by hand is the bottleneck. Several packages in one repository, each with its own tag, is its strength.
x-selection.limits: The bump comes from commit MESSAGES, not from what changed: a `feat:` that removed something gives a minor bump. Check it against the surface diff (skill step 1). With the default token it cannot open PRs unless the repository allows Actions to. It needs a config file (`--config-file`); a missing one falls back to defaults that find nothing. The tag appears only when its release PR is merged.
x-selection.cost: Not configured here. One config file and one manifest per repository; each run is a few seconds of API calls.

post.summary: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
post.description: Lay down each declared remote mount — a `source.remote` layer in the root `index.config.json`, or, in a folio with no index, a `remoteMounts` entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, `index.lock.json` (a legacy `<name>.mount-lock.json` is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root `.gitignore` block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through `writeDeclaredMounts` into `index.config.json`. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (`schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts`, rule H8): a person's consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. `--staging` mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or `mountDefaults` names may be one the layer declares in its `<name>.json` or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (`skills/skills.json` naming `voices`), resolved at the pin through `instanceDirectories`; an id in neither is refused at plan time. `tools` on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (`<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts`), its implementation (the `inProcess.module`, or the script its `bun run cat <key>` resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools' `importClosure` (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A `hydrated` mount lays each chosen directory down as its published `index.hydrated.jsonld` only: read from the pin's git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin's subgraph index package (the `subgraph-index-<sha>` release asset `subgraph-index-package` publishes), its tarball checked against its `folio-binary-release/v1` record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, `SubgraphHydratedSchema` and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package's URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. `--check` compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. When a run CHANGES the lock, it then re-renders the agent surface (`skill:commands` → `.claude/commands/`, `agent-memory` → `.claude/agent-memory/` and `.agents/`) from the checkout root, so a re-pin commit carries the skills and memory the new layers define; a generator that fails fails the run, and `--no-agent-surface` opts out.

instance.description: The downstream layer root; omitted, every declaring layer in the checkout.

staging.description: Mount for a staging preview: no signature or consent required.

check.description: Compare the disk against the lock; fetch nothing.

noAgentSurface.description: Do not re-render `.claude/commands/` and the agent memory after a mount that changed the lock.

noInstall.description: Lay the pinned bytes down without `bun install` in each mounted layer that carries a `package.json`. By default the install runs (`--production`; `--install-all` keeps devDependencies), so the mounted tools run; it writes only `node_modules/`, which no mount digest covers, so `--check` still passes.

seed.description: `<name>=<owner/repo>@<40-char sha>`: create or re-pin that remote layer in `index.config.json` instead of mounting, writing its `trust.consent` for that pin in the same write (needs `consentBy` and `evidence`; repeatable; `--whole` mounts every tracked file). Refused while a mount it moves has edits the lock does not hold, since the next mount would leave that mount at the old commit; `fresh` lets it through.

fresh.description: Replace a mount whose bytes no longer hash to the lock instead of leaving it untouched; with `seed`, re-pin over such edits. The edits are discarded.

choose.description: `<harness>[:<instance>]`: write a review's choice (`directories` and/or `tools`) into that mount entry's `overrides.<instance>` instead of mounting, so a fresh clone replays it. The pin and its consent are untouched; the next mount resolves the choice and the lock records what it resolved to.

directories.description: With `choose`: comma-separated directory ids, nested ids or concern names.

tools.description: With `choose`: comma-separated Tool ids, each mounted runnable.

evidence.description: With `seed`: where the consent was given, readable (a session, an issue comment), as `consent.evidence`. On stdin because it is free prose: it quotes what was said.

outcomes.description: Per layer: mounted, local, skipped, missing (including refused by the trust gate) or could-not-determine.

post.summary: Record what the publish branch served
post.description: Append one entry to the render log on the publish branch: what was published or taken down, when, from which commit, and — for a removal or a retention — WHY. The log is the only place a preview that vanished leaves a trace.

dir.description: A checkout of the publish branch, or a publish directory about to become one. This tool NEVER fetches, commits or pushes: the calling workflows hold the checkout with their own retry and concurrency handling, and a second pusher racing them could lose a deploy.

event.description: `rendered`, `removed`, `restored` or `retained`. `retained` records a removal CONSIDERED and refused, which would otherwise leave no trace.

kind.description: What was rendered — `staging-preview`, `site`, `export`. Open, not an enum: the publish branch carries more than previews, and an enum would make logging a new kind wait on a schema change.

path.description: The path on the publish branch. Checked as a VALUE, never trusted by provenance: the slug sanitiser can emit `..`, which is only safe for a slug taken from a git ref, and a dispatch input is not one.

slug.description: The staging slug, where the subject has one.

branch.description: The branch the render came from.

commit.description: The commit the artefact was built from.

run.description: The workflow run that wrote this, so a reader can open the log.

prose.description: One JSON object on STDIN: `{summary, reason?, detail?, format?}`. `summary` is required and one line. `reason` is required by the SCRIPT for `removed` and `retained`, because an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity the log exists to prevent. `format` declares how the prose reads (absent means plain text, never sniffed). Build it with `jq -n --arg`, never by concatenation.

entry.description: The day's JSONL the entry was APPENDED to. Append is the only verb: there is no `--remove`, no `--edit` and no `--id`, so a takedown is a `removed` ENTRY rather than the erasure of the `rendered` one before it, and the never-delete rule is structural rather than a guard every cleanup path must remember.

x-selection.when: Whenever something is published to or removed from the publish branch — including a removal that was refused. Called from `feature-staging.yml` at four points; `staging-render-log.bpmn` is the process.
x-selection.limits: It writes into a directory and does not push, so a caller that forgets to commit the log has written nothing durable. It cannot edit or delete an entry, by design. `--summary` / `--reason` / `--detail` are REFUSED as flags at exit 2 rather than ignored: they go on stdin, and a caller still passing them is told instead of silently logging an entry with no summary.
x-selection.cost: One appended line. No network.

post.summary: The render pipeline, in dependency order
post.description: Flatten the repository's renders into the order their `needs` imply, and optionally run them. Two stages: the current declared state as json/jsonld and the README derived from it are FATAL; the dynamic renderers (viewers, visualisers, doc pages, diagrams) skip and log; the dynamic-state export closes it. A cycle or a missing dependency yields NO order rather than a partial one.

dry_run.description: Print the flattened order and each step's failure policy without running anything.

report.description: Per step: ran, failed, skipped, or PENDING — declared with no implementation yet, which is never rendered as a pass.

post.summary: Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes
post.description: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled `no-sheet` and, with `--author`, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints `{"status":"unchanged"}` and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column `@login (#N): first paragraph`, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked `closed`), and `closedRows`, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled `change-set` unless `--label` says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an `issue-unlinked` change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With `--accept` it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against.

repo.description: The folio repository, `owner/name`, whose issues, open and closed, are read with `gh api`.

sheet.description: The Contributor Feedback tab's values (a public-comment log: Review Change Sets) as JSON: the Sheets API `values` array (or the whole `get_values` answer), from row 1, so the header row (first cell `Change-set`) is found.

state.description: The last check's state file. Missing on the first check, which reports every open issue as opened.

issues.description: Issues as JSON (the issues API's shape), instead of reading them with `gh api`. For tests and offline runs.

author.description: Only issues this GitHub login opened. Default every author.

sheetHash.description: The sheet script's hash of the person-set cells, Watch!G1. Given, it stands for the cells, so `--sheet` needs only the header row and the Issue column.

label.description: Only issues with this label, e.g. `change-set`. Default every issue on a read with an Issue column, and `change-set` on one without (a public-comment log).

skipLabel.description: The label that keeps an issue off the sheet. Default `no-sheet`.

result.description: JSON on standard output: `status` (`unchanged` or `changed`), `digest`, and when changed `changes`, `append` (rows aligned to the header, each with `closed`), `closedRows` and `state`. Exit 0 unchanged, 10 changed, 2 usage.

x-selection.when: On every poll of a review-log watcher, before any agent work: the agent pass runs only when this reports `changed`.
x-selection.limits: Reads one tab and one repository's issues; it never writes the sheet or GitHub. It sees an edit only in the watched headers, so the agent's own Green columns and the script's Grey ones never wake the watcher.
x-selection.cost: One `gh api` call per 100 issues and one small JSON file; well under a second.

post.summary: Build the review sheet's Apps Script and a document's Config tab
post.description: Builds `Code.gs` (`--script`), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from `review-sheet.gs`), and one document's Config tab rows (`--config`), filled from the folio's `review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json`, its review anchors and the draft's `pdf-line-map.json`. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet's links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each `No. n` linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document's URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet's Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs `installTriggers`; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With `"mode": "drafting"` in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document's table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab.

script.description: Where to write the generic Code.gs. The same for every document.

repo.description: The folio repository. Default the current directory.

config.description: The folio's sheet settings, e.g. `review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json`: anchors, lineMap, draftUrl, commentUrl, and optional namedSections, aliases, tabs and columns. A drafting sheet's config (`review/drafting/sheet-sync.json`) has mode `drafting`, anchors and sectionUrl.

out.description: Where to write the Config tab's rows (JSON). Default standard output.

script.description: Code.gs, ready to paste into any review sheet's Apps Script editor. Never committed: it is rebuilt from the template.

configRows.description: The Config tab's rows for one document, which the agent writes into the sheet. Never committed: rebuilt from the config.

x-install.service: Google Apps Script bound to the review sheet: copy the template, have the agent write its Config tab, add editors to the "Ready columns: editors" lock, paste Code.gs, run installTriggers (skill review-sheet-script, "Setting up a sheet for a new document")

x-selection.when: A public review is kept in a shared Google Sheet with the public-comment tabs (Review Public Comments, Review Change Sets, Agent - Comments, Agent - Change Sets), and its links or joined columns must stay current without an agent re-pasting them. Also after the review anchors, the draft's link prefix or a tab or column name changes: rewrite the Config tab (the script stays).
x-selection.limits: Builds the script only; installing it is a person's step in the sheet, since the sheet's owner must authorise it. It reads only the tabs and headers named in the config. In the reviewers' columns the link text must be in the cell already: it links what reviewers wrote and does not rewrite their words. The joined columns and Agentic status it writes whole.
x-selection.cost: Reads three JSON files and writes one file of about 20 kB. In the sheet, a full refresh of 800 rows takes about 20 seconds.

post.summary: Rewrite paths that still name a moved file's old layer — never in a record
post.description: After a move between two layers lands, find every mention `<from>/<prefix>/<rest>` in the scanned tree's tracked files and rewrite it to `<to>/<prefix>/<rest>` only when the file exists under the destination root and not under the source root. Records are never read: beans, todos, memory, proposals, wireframes, QA results, upstream pins, vocab mappings, provenance figures and terminologies, and test fixtures (`DEFAULT_RECORD_GLOBS`; the CLI's `--keep <glob>` adds more, generated trees among them, which their generators rewrite — a glob is not a shell-safe argument type, so it is not a declared input). Reports by default with file and line; `--write` applies; `--check` exits 1 while a rewrite is owed.

fromName.description: The moved files' old layer, as paths spell it (e.g. the harness).

toName.description: The layer the files moved to.

scan.description: The git checkout whose tracked files are read; default the source root.

check.description: Exit 1 while any rewrite is owed; write nothing.

rewrites.description: Rewrites made or owed, each with file and line; mentions left alone; record files not read.

post.description: Render each skill's input/output JSON Schema as a browsable Markdown reference page, with an index. The generated pages are committed so they are readable on the forge as well as on the site.

check.description: Compare against the committed pages and fail if stale, instead of writing.

schemaReference.description: The generated reference directory. Never hand-edited.

post.description: Render each declared schema directory as a page per subject layer, over one shared data index.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.summary: Check an IG's built Questionnaires with CSIRO's SDC libraries
post.description: Build-time Structured Data Capture checks, one result per Questionnaire (`sdcChecks[]` of `fhir-questionnaire-wireframe`): `assemble` (`@aehrc/sdc-assemble` 2.0.3: an assemble-root's sub-forms resolve in this IG, and `--out` writes the assembled Questionnaire), `template-extract` (`@aehrc/sdc-template-extract` 1.0.16: extraction from the IG's fixture response yields the expected resources), `populate` (`@aehrc/sdc-populate` 4.7.2: FHIRPath pre-population from a fixture context gives the expected answers) and `behaviour` (`@aehrc/questionnaire-test-toolkit` 0.1.0: the IG's own behavioural test, warn-only). Checks only, no UI.

ast.description: The IG's FHIR AST (`output-ast/`): its Questionnaires, and the canonicals a sub-form resolves against.

questionnaire.description: A Questionnaire id to check; default every one in the AST.

out.description: Where assembled Questionnaires are written.

sdcChecks.description: Per Questionnaire, per check: pass, fail, not-applicable, no-fixture or could-not-determine — the last three never a pass. JSON with `--json`. Exit 1 on an error-severity failure; behavioural tests never fail the run.

x-selection.when: After SUSHI has built the IG's Questionnaires and before they are reviewed as forms; whenever a Questionnaire uses modular sub-forms, template extraction or pre-population.
x-selection.limits: Only as good as the IG's fixtures: with none, extraction and population say `no-fixture` rather than pass. Nothing is fetched from a server: sub-forms resolve in the AST and population queries in the fixture. The behavioural toolkit is early and needs React and Smart Forms peers installed with the IG's tests; without them it is `could-not-determine`, a warning.
x-selection.cost: Seconds per Questionnaire; a behavioural test runs a bun test process.

post.summary: Lexical search over the content graph
post.description: Find graph nodes, authored or ingested, whose label, title, kind or tags contain a string, with no graph expansion. corpus-search composes this with a neighbour walk.

result.description: JSON: the matching nodes and which field matched.

post.summary: Check declared credential needs against workflow use and expiry, by name
post.description: Compare each repository's declared credential needs (`credentials/needs.json`, profile and registry) with the `secrets.NAME` expressions its workflows reference (GitHub Actions' dollar-and-double-brace form, said in words because this text is rendered on a Jekyll page), with the secret names GitHub lists when a token allows it, and with any recorded expiry. NAMES ONLY — no value is ever read. Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0.

repos.description: Repository checkouts to check. Default: every repository the index mounts.

json.description: Print the result as JSON instead of the human report.

verdict.description: The exit status: 0 clean, 1 a major or critical finding, 2 could not determine.

x-selection.when: Before relying on a workflow's credentials, or to see which secrets a repository needs, uses and lacks.
x-selection.limits: Presence on GitHub is judged only when a token may list secret names (`list-secret-names`); without one that half is could-not-determine, never clean.
x-selection.cost: Reads workflow and declaration files; one API call per repository when a token is present.

post.summary: Run every existing security check as one named release step
post.description: Run the repository's security checks — workflow injection, secret leaks, lockfile pinning, the toolchain pin, QA reviewer permission, materialised-asset fixity — plus two advisories (dependency advisories, third-party action SHA pinning), each by name as argv. Every check is reported as pass, fail or unknown; a blocking check that fails OR could not be run refuses the release, because could-not-check is never clean. Advisories are reported and never block. Called by `prepare-merge` before a push that will merge, and by any publish process before it publishes.

json.description: Print a `folio-security-gate/v1` result on stdout instead of the human report.

blocked.description: Whether a blocking check failed or could not be run; also the exit status (1 when blocked).

post.summary: Is this repository's cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
post.description: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: `mounts` (every declared layer on disk at its pin — `remote-mount --check`), `declarations` (every path a declaration names resolves — `declaration-resolution`), `monorepo-paths` (no wiring still names the monorepo: `livesAt` on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), `import-direction` and `reference-direction` (no layer reaches a layer above it), and `site` (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — `build-instance-site --no-mount`, only with `--site`). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without `--site` the answer is never 0.

root.description: The separated checkout. Default: the working directory.

site.description: Build the site from the mounts on disk (minutes); without it the `site` condition is not run and the verdict cannot be complete.

monorepo.description: The repository the separation left, `<owner>/<repo>`. Default: litlfred/folio-assistant.

monorepoDir.description: Its old checkout directory name, as paths spell it. Default: the repository's name.

json.description: Print the report as JSON, mounted-layer findings included.

conditions.description: Per condition: pass, fail, could-not-determine or not-run, the gate that decided it, and its findings.

x-selection.when: Before calling a separation's cutover (kg-separation stage 13) done, and after any re-pin of a separated repository's layers.
x-selection.limits: It judges ONE repository. A downstream's own CI and the parent repository's retirement are not observed from here.
x-selection.cost: Seconds without `--site`; a full Jekyll build with it.

post.description: Serve a layer's renderings over local HTTP with their declared media types. The publication host wherever GitHub Pages is absent, and the only host that can enforce `application/ld+json` at all.

directory.description: Tree to serve; defaults to the built site when present.

port.description: 0 binds a free port, which is what the tests use.

url.description: Where the tree is being served.

x-selection.when: Serving renderings in a Bun / JavaScript / TypeScript runtime environment.

post.summary: Publish a folio's or an IG's site from the agent's own checkout — the one agent publish path
post.description: Build a repository's site in the agent's checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared `site.build` recipe (built by `build-instance-site`), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — `folio-staging.yml` for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG's `ghbuild.yml` for a FHIR IG, whose `build` job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (`sync-docs-harness`, then `rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>`): every page gains the rail and the icon row `#fa-navbar-row`, and the IG's own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose `index.html` wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; `--plan` stops there, `--dry-run` composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, `--artifact` writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead.

Without a `site.build` recipe an IG falls back to its own workflow's Publisher steps, which need a Docker daemon and give the rail and icon row only.

post.summary: Where to drop a file — the queue's upload URL
post.description: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer's own declaration: the `uploads` graph's directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub's `/upload/<branch>/<path>`. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared `uploads` graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no `origin` remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the LAYER and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404.

branch.description: The branch the upload form targets. Defaults to `main`; pass the working branch to send somebody to a pull request's head instead, so the upload lands on a commit CI judges.

url.description: The upload URL on stdout, exit 0 — or, on stderr and exit 1, the reason it could not be composed and the remedy for that reason. Never a guessed URL: a URL is believed, and somebody sent to a wrong one cannot tell it from an empty directory.

x-selection.when: You are about to tell somebody where to put a file, in any channel. Reach for it every time, not only when unsure: a hand-written path breaks silently when a directory moves. It also answers "which queue" when a checkout declares more than one (one per layer): the answer is whichever layer root you pass, never a literal.
x-selection.limits: It answers WHERE, and nothing else. It does not upload, does not check whether the person has write access, and cannot tell you which of several declared queues should own a given file — that is undecided and `upload-routes` says so rather than picking. The `/upload/<branch>/<path>` form is GitHub's, so another forge gets a named refusal rather than a guess. And the URL it hands back opens the route with the FEWEST guarantees: the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator run happen on it, and everything `upload-routes` lists has to be discharged afterwards from a checkout.
x-selection.cost: One read of the declaration and one of the git remote; no network at run time and nothing installed.

For each viewport it records `script` entries for renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each pass or fail with a note. It writes a screenshot per viewport and a report.json carrying the use, topic and surface, and exits 1 on any fail and 2 when the candidate set is not one the use admits.

Also lists files that are not strict JSON, which Python's reader accepts and every other consumer rejects. Report-only: it never edits a witness, which is generator output.

post.description: Re-run a computation witness's producer and say whether it reproduces the committed witness. Reads the command from `invocation.reproduce` (else `python3 <scriptFile>`) and the recorded package versions from `environment`; on a version mismatch it stops at `unknown`, since a different environment is not a reproduction test. Otherwise it runs the COMMITTED producer in a scratch git worktree, so the folio's own checkout is never written, and compares the result with the committed witness with run-specific fields (commit, timing, environment) masked at every depth. `pass`, `fail` (with the differing JSON paths), or `unknown` (mismatch, non-zero exit, timeout, no witness written).

force.description: Run despite an environment mismatch; the verdict is then marked advisory.

Copied inline as `definitions.stagingLinks` into every skill contract that carries it; schemas/staging.test.ts fails when a copy drifts.

branch.description: Feature branch name.

slug.description: Branch slug used in the staging URL path.

pages.description: One entry per changed page, deep-linked; from the change's rendered-impact list, never chosen by judgement.

before.description: Same page on main; absent for a new page.

after.description: The page on the staging preview, with the anchor where the change sits; absent for a deleted page.

summary.description: What to look at on this page.

missing.description: What could not be linked, said rather than hidden: no preview yet (and when it will exist), no page list computed, or a changed page the publish ref does not hold.

skill.wireframe-viewport-check.output.st.$comment: Copy of cat-harness schemas/staging-comparison.schema.json; cat-harness schemas/staging.test.ts fails when a copy drifts.

SurfaceRef.description: A rendered surface: a visualiser route key such as cat-harness/beans, or a kebab-case name such as navbar.

Text.description: A short single-line human string. Not admissible as a command-line argument.

TimeWindow.description: A history window: a count with a unit (4h, 2d, 1w) or an ISO date.

WireframeUse.description: Why a wireframe is drawn: `design` for a new or changed surface, `as-is` for an existing visualiser.

WorkbookPath.description: A repository path to a spreadsheet workbook.
